370	            avg_done_s=gavg,
371	            eta_s=eta,
372	            status_breakdown=gbreakdown,
373	            failed_task_ids=failed_ids,
374	        ))
375	
376	    overall_eta_candidates = [g.eta_s for g in group_recs if g.eta_s is not None]
377	    overall_eta = max(overall_eta_candidates) if overall_eta_candidates else None
378	
379	    host = socket.gethostname().split(".")[0] or "host"
380	    return HostSnapshot(
381	        host=host,
382	        daemon_reachable=True,
383	        error=None,
384	        total_tasks=total,
385	        total_done=done,
386	        overall_pct=overall_pct,
387	        avg_done_s=avg_done,
388	        eta_s=overall_eta,
389	        status_breakdown=status_breakdown,
390	        groups=group_recs,
391	        tasks=tasks,
392	    )
393

395	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
396	# Text rendering — ports 36_pueue.zsh
397	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
398	def _fmt_duration(s: float | None) -> str:
399	    if s is None:
400	        return "-"
401	    s_int = int(s)
402	    if s_int < 60:
403	        return f"{s_int}s"
404	    if s_int < 3600:
405	        return f"{s_int // 60}m {s_int % 60}s"
406	    return f"{s_int // 3600}h {(s_int % 3600) // 60}m {s_int % 60}s"
407	
408	
409	def _fmt_pct(p: float) -> str:
410	    return f"{round(p * 10) / 10:.1f}%"
411	
412	
413	def _progress_bar(pct: float, width: int = 12) -> str:
414	    p = max(0, min(100, int(round(pct))))
415	    filled = p * width // 100
416	    empty = width - filled
417	    return "[" + "=" * filled + "-" * empty + "]"
418	
419	
420	def _breakdown_str(b: dict[str, int]) -> str:
421	    if not b:
422	        return "-"
423	    return ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in sorted(b.items()))
424	
425	
426	def render_text(snap: HostSnapshot, use_color: bool) -> None:
427	    out = Console(force_terminal=use_color, no_color=not use_color, soft_wrap=True)
428	    title = Text("Pueue Summary", style="bold cyan" if use_color else "")
429	    out.print(title)
430	    out.print(Text("Overall", style="bold cyan" if use_color else ""))
431	    out.print(f"  Total tasks: {snap.total_tasks}")
432	    bar = _progress_bar(snap.overall_pct)
433	    out.print(f"  Done progress: {snap.total_done}/{snap.total_tasks}  {bar}  {_fmt_pct(snap.overall_pct)}")
434	    out.print(f"  Avg done duration: {_fmt_duration(snap.avg_done_s)}")
435	    out.print(f"  Est. remaining (ETA): {_fmt_duration(snap.eta_s)}")
436	    out.print()
437	    out.print(Text("Status Breakdown", style="bold cyan" if use_color else ""))
438	    if not snap.status_breakdown:
439	        out.print("  -")
440	    else:
441	        tbl = Table(show_header=True, header_style="bold", box=None, pad_edge=False)
442	        tbl.add_column("status")
443	        tbl.add_column("count", justify="right")
444	        tbl.add_column("progress", justify="right")
445	        for k, v in sorted(snap.status_breakdown.items()):
446	            pct = (v * 100 / snap.total_tasks) if snap.total_tasks else 0.0
447	            tbl.add_row(k, str(v), _fmt_pct(pct))
448	        out.print(tbl)
449	    out.print()
450	    out.print(Text("Group Summary", style="bold cyan" if use_color else ""))
451	    if not snap.groups:
452	        out.print("  -")
453	        return
454	    gtbl = Table(show_header=True, header_style="bold", box=None, pad_edge=False)
455	    for col in ("group", "daemon", "parallel", "total", "done", "progress", "bar", "total_spent", "avg_done", "eta", "statuses"):
456	        gtbl.add_column(col)
457	    for g in snap.groups:
458	        gtbl.add_row(
459	            g.name,
460	            g.daemon_status,
461	            str(g.parallel_tasks),
462	            str(g.total),
463	            str(g.done),
464	            _fmt_pct(g.pct),
465	            _progress_bar(g.pct),
466	            _fmt_duration(g.total_spent_s),
467	            _fmt_duration(g.avg_done_s),
468	            _fmt_duration(g.eta_s),
469	            _breakdown_str(g.status_breakdown),
470	        )
471	    out.print(gtbl)
472

474	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
475	# AI prompt + cache
476	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
477	PROMPT_PREAMBLE = """\
478	You are summarizing a developer's pueue (https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue) \
479	task-queue state so they can quickly see what's running, what's safe to \
480	clean up, and what failures need recovery action. Input: one or more host \
481	snapshots from `pueue status --json`, post-parsed (envs stripped).
482	
483	For EACH host, and within it EACH group, infer:
484	  1. summary (<= 80 chars): what kind of work the queue is doing. Name the \
485	project or task pattern if visible from command strings (e.g. "3 sklearn \
486	sweeps", "2 ffmpeg encodes"). Avoid generic "tasks running".
487	  2. cleanability tier:
488	     "safe-to-clean" → all tasks are Done with result Success, last task \
489	ended >2 hours ago, no Running/Queued/Paused/Stashed. The user can run \
490	`pueue clean -g <group>` to free the slate without losing useful state.
491	     "review" → mixed Done+Failed, OR any Done with non-Success result, OR \
492	last task ended <2h ago, OR Stashed/Paused present, OR uncertain. User \
493	should look before cleaning.
494	     "keep" → has Running/Queued, or fresh failure (<10 min) with no \
495	recovery hint yet, or task list referenced by `--after` dependencies that \
496	are still pending.
497	  3. cleanability_reason (<= 60 chars): one-line WHY for the tier.
498	  4. cleanup_command: an exact shell command. For safe-to-clean use \
499	`pueue clean -g <group>`. For review/keep emit empty string.
500	
501	For EACH Failed task (status=Done with non-Success result, OR status=Killed):
502	  - summary (<= 60 chars): what went wrong, e.g. "OOM at epoch 3", "exit 1 \
503	on missing config file".
504	  - recovery_hint (<= 100 chars): concrete advice. Apply these heuristics:
505	     a. Same command as a successful later task in the same group → \
506	"already covered by task N (succeeded with same args)".
507	     b. Exit code 124 (timeout) → "increase --timeout, then pueue restart".
508	     c. Exit code 137 (OOM-kill) → "increase memory; pueue restart with \
509	larger limit".
510	     d. Exit code 143 (SIGTERM) → "transient; pueue restart".
511	     e. Multiple consecutive failures with same exit code → "group/env \
512	misconfig, not per-task; investigate before retrying".
513	     f. Stale Paused (>24h) → "stale; pueue start or pueue remove".
514	     g. Otherwise → "inspect `pueue log <id>` for cause".
515	  - recovery_command: the suggested shell command (or empty string).
516	
517	Be conservative. When in doubt between cleanability tiers, pick the \
518	SAFER one (keep > review > safe-to-clean). False keep is recoverable; \
519	false safe-to-clean destroys task history.
520	
521	Respond with STRICT JSON only (no prose, no fences):
522	{
523	  "hosts": [
524	    {
525	      "host": "<hostname>",
526	      "daemon": "<Running|Paused|N/A>",
527	      "groups": [
528	        {
529	          "name": "<group>",
530	          "summary": "<<=80 chars>",
531	          "cleanability": "safe-to-clean" | "review" | "keep",
532	          "cleanability_reason": "<<=60 chars>",
533	          "cleanup_command": "<exact shell or empty>",
534	          "tasks_highlight": [
535	            {"id": <int>, "status": "<Done|Failed|Running|...>",
536	             "summary": "<<=60 chars>",
537	             "recovery_hint": "<<=100 chars or empty>",
538	             "recovery_command": "<exact shell or empty>"}
539	          ]
540	        }
541	      ],
542	      "overall_summary": "<<=120 chars one-line summary for this host>"
543	    }
544	  ],
545	  "fleet_summary": "<<=160 chars one-line summary across all hosts; empty if single host>"
546	}
547	"""
548	
549	
550	def _host_to_ai_input(snap: HostSnapshot) -> dict:
551	    def task_brief(t: TaskRec) -> dict:
552	        cmd = t.command if len(t.command) <= 200 else (t.command[:200] + "…")
553	        return {
554	            "id": t.id,
555	            "status": t.status,
556	            "result": t.result,
557	            "exit_code": t.exit_code,
558	            "group": t.group,
559	            "command": cmd,
560	            "label": t.label,
561	            "created_at": t.created_at,
562	            "start": t.start,
563	            "end": t.end,
564	            "duration_s": round(t.duration_s, 2) if t.duration_s is not None else None,
565	        }
566	    # Limit task volume sent to LLM: all non-Done tasks, plus last 5 Done per group.
567	    selected: list[TaskRec] = []
568	    by_group: dict[str, list[TaskRec]] = {}
569	    for t in snap.tasks:
570	        if t.status != "Done" or (t.result and t.result != "Success"):
571	            selected.append(t)
572	        else:
573	            by_group.setdefault(t.group, []).append(t)
574	    for g_tasks in by_group.values():
575	        g_tasks.sort(key=lambda t: t.end or "")
576	        selected.extend(g_tasks[-5:])
577	    return {
578	        "host": snap.host,
579	        "daemon_reachable": snap.daemon_reachable,
580	        "error": snap.error,
581	        "groups": [
582	            {
583	                "name": g.name,
584	                "daemon_status": g.daemon_status,
585	                "parallel_tasks": g.parallel_tasks,
586	                "total": g.total,
587	                "done": g.done,
588	                "pct": round(g.pct, 1),
589	                "status_breakdown": g.status_breakdown,
590	                "eta_s": round(g.eta_s, 1) if g.eta_s is not None else None,
591	                "avg_done_s": round(g.avg_done_s, 1) if g.avg_done_s is not None else None,
592	            }
593	            for g in snap.groups
594	        ],
595	        "tasks": [task_brief(t) for t in selected],
596	    }
597	
598	
599	def build_prompt(snapshots: list[HostSnapshot], multi_host: bool) -> str:
600	    payload = {
601	        "multi_host": multi_host,
602	        "hosts": [_host_to_ai_input(s) for s in snapshots],
603	    }
604	    return PROMPT_PREAMBLE + "\n--- INPUT ---\n" + json.dumps(payload, indent=2, default=str) + "\nReturn JSON now.\n"
605	
606	
607	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
608	# Cache
609	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
610	_CACHE_VERSION = "v1"
611	
612	
613	def _cache_path(prompt_hash: str) -> Path:
614	    base = os.environ.get("XDG_CACHE_HOME") or os.path.expanduser("~/.cache")
615	    d = Path(base) / "pqsum"
616	    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
617	    host = socket.gethostname().split(".")[0] or "host"
618	    return d / f"{host}-{prompt_hash}.json"
619	
620	
621	def _cache_lookup(prompt_hash: str) -> tuple[dict | None, str]:
622	    p = _cache_path(prompt_hash)
623	    if not p.is_file():
624	        return None, "miss"
625	    try:
626	        data = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
627	    except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
628	        return None, "miss"
629	    if data.get("version") != _CACHE_VERSION:
630	        return None, "miss"
631	    if data.get("prompt_hash") != prompt_hash:
632	        return None, "miss"
633	    age = time.time() - float(data.get("generated_at", 0))
634	    parsed = data.get("parsed")
635	    if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
636	        return None, "miss"
637	    if age > PQSUM_MIN_REFRESH_INTERVAL > 0:
638	        return parsed, "stale-hit"
639	    return parsed, "hit"
640	
641	
642	def _cache_save(prompt_hash: str, parsed: dict) -> None:
643	    p = _cache_path(prompt_hash)
644	    try:
645	        p.write_text(json.dumps({
646	            "version": _CACHE_VERSION,
647	            "prompt_hash": prompt_hash,
648	            "generated_at": time.time(),
649	            "parsed": parsed,
650	        }, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
651	    except OSError as e:
652	        err.print(f"[yellow]pqsum: cache write failed: {e}[/yellow]")
653

655	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
656	# Agent invocation
657	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
658	def detect_agent() -> str | None:
659	    if AICAP_AGENT:
660	        if AICAP_AGENT == "http" or shutil.which(AICAP_AGENT):
661	            return AICAP_AGENT
662	        err.print(f"[red]AICAP_AGENT={AICAP_AGENT!r} but that CLI isn't on PATH.[/red]")
663	        return None
664	    for cand in AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY:
665	        if shutil.which(cand):
666	            return cand
667	    return None
668	
669	
670	def model_for(agent: str) -> str:
671	    return {
672	        "claude": AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL or "(default)",
673	        "opencode": AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL or "(default)",
674	        "codex": AICAP_CODEX_MODEL or "(default)",
675	        "agyc": "(account)",
676	        "cursor-agent": AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL or "(default)",
677	        "http": AICAP_HTTP_MODEL,
678	    }.get(agent, "?")
679	
680	
681	def invoke_agent(agent: str, prompt: str, timeout: float) -> str:
682	    if agent == "http":
683	        return _invoke_http(prompt, timeout)
684	    base = AGENT_CONFIG[agent]["base"]
685	    try:
686	        result = subprocess.run([*base, prompt], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
687	    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
688	        err.print(f"[red]{agent} timed out after {timeout:.0f}s[/red]")
689	        return ""
690	    except FileNotFoundError:
691	        err.print(f"[red]{agent} not on PATH (race vs detect_agent)[/red]")
692	        return ""
693	    if result.returncode != 0:
694	        err.print(f"[red]{agent} exited {result.returncode}[/red]")
695	        if result.stderr.strip():
696	            err.print(f"[dim]{result.stderr.strip()[:500]}[/dim]")
697	        return ""
698	    return result.stdout
699	
700	
701	def _invoke_http(prompt: str, timeout: float) -> str:
702	    payload = json.dumps({
703	        "model": AICAP_HTTP_MODEL,
704	        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
705	        "stream": False,
706	    }).encode("utf-8")
707	    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
708	    if AICAP_HTTP_API_KEY:
709	        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {AICAP_HTTP_API_KEY}"
710	    req = urllib.request.Request(AICAP_HTTP_URL, data=payload, headers=headers, method="POST")
711	    try:
712	        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:
713	            body = resp.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
714	    except (urllib.error.HTTPError, urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError) as e:
715	        err.print(f"[red]http: {e}[/red]")
716	        return ""
717	    try:
718	        parsed = json.loads(body)
719	        return parsed["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
720	    except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, IndexError, TypeError):
721	        err.print(f"[red]http: unexpected response shape[/red] [dim]{body[:300]}[/dim]")
722	        return ""
723	
724	
725	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
726	# AI response parsing
727	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
728	_TIERS = ("safe-to-clean", "review", "keep")
729	
730	
731	def parse_reply(reply: str) -> dict | None:
732	    if not reply.strip():
733	        return None
734	    s = reply.strip()
735	    if s.startswith("```"):
736	        s = s.split("\n", 1)[1] if "\n" in s else s
737	        if s.endswith("```"):
738	            s = s.rsplit("```", 1)[0]
739	        s = s.strip()
740	    start, end = s.find("{"), s.rfind("}")
741	    if start == -1 or end == -1 or end < start:
742	        return None
743	    try:
744	        parsed = json.loads(s[start:end + 1])
745	    except json.JSONDecodeError:
746	        return None
747	    if not isinstance(parsed, dict) or not isinstance(parsed.get("hosts"), list):
748	        return None
749	
750	    cleaned_hosts: list[dict] = []
751	    for h in parsed["hosts"]:
752	        if not isinstance(h, dict):
753	            continue
754	        groups_out: list[dict] = []
755	        for g in (h.get("groups") or []):
756	            if not isinstance(g, dict):
757	                continue
758	            tier = str(g.get("cleanability", "")).strip().lower()
759	            if tier not in _TIERS:
760	                tier = "keep"
761	            highlights: list[dict] = []
762	            for t in (g.get("tasks_highlight") or []):
763	                if not isinstance(t, dict):
764	                    continue
765	                tid_raw = t.get("id")
766	                try:
767	                    tid = int(tid_raw) if tid_raw is not None else -1
768	                except (TypeError, ValueError):
769	                    tid = -1
770	                highlights.append({
771	                    "id": tid,
772	                    "status": str(t.get("status", "")).strip()[:30],
773	                    "summary": str(t.get("summary", "")).strip()[:200],
774	                    "recovery_hint": str(t.get("recovery_hint", "")).strip()[:200],
775	                    "recovery_command": str(t.get("recovery_command", "")).strip()[:500],
776	                })
777	            groups_out.append({
778	                "name": str(g.get("name", "")).strip()[:80],
779	                "summary": str(g.get("summary", "")).strip()[:200],
780	                "cleanability": tier,
781	                "cleanability_reason": str(g.get("cleanability_reason", "")).strip()[:200],
782	                "cleanup_command": str(g.get("cleanup_command", "")).strip()[:500],
783	                "tasks_highlight": highlights[:5],
784	            })
785	        cleaned_hosts.append({
786	            "host": str(h.get("host", "")).strip()[:80],
787	            "daemon": str(h.get("daemon", "")).strip()[:30],
788	            "groups": groups_out,
789	            "overall_summary": str(h.get("overall_summary", "")).strip()[:300],
790	        })
791	    return {
792	        "hosts": cleaned_hosts,
793	        "fleet_summary": str(parsed.get("fleet_summary", "")).strip()[:400],
794	    }
795	
796	
797	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
798	# AI rendering — Rich blocks
799	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
800	_TIER_GLYPHS = {"safe-to-clean": "🟢", "review": "🟡", "keep": "🔴"}
801	_TIER_COLORS = {"safe-to-clean": "green", "review": "yellow", "keep": "red"}
802	
803	
804	def render_ai(parsed: dict, use_color: bool) -> None:
805	    out = Console(force_terminal=use_color, no_color=not use_color, soft_wrap=True)
806	    fleet = parsed.get("fleet_summary") or ""
807	    if fleet:
808	        out.print(Text(f"🌐 {fleet}", style="bold cyan" if use_color else ""))
809	        out.print()
810	    for h in parsed.get("hosts", []):
811	        host = h.get("host", "?")
812	        daemon = h.get("daemon", "?")
813	        header = Text()
814	        header.append(f"▶ {host}", style="bold")
815	        header.append(f"  daemon={daemon}", style="dim")
816	        out.print(header)
817	        ov = h.get("overall_summary", "")
818	        if ov:
819	            out.print(Text(f"  {ov}", style="dim italic"))
820	        for g in h.get("groups", []):
821	            tier = g.get("cleanability", "keep")
822	            glyph = _TIER_GLYPHS.get(tier, "⚪")
823	            color = _TIER_COLORS.get(tier, "white")
824	            line = Text()
825	            line.append(f"  {glyph} ", style="bold")
826	            line.append(f"{g.get('name', '?')}", style=f"bold {color}")
827	            line.append(f"  {g.get('summary', '')}", style="white")
828	            reason = g.get("cleanability_reason", "")
829	            if reason:
830	                line.append(f"  ({reason})", style="dim italic")
831	            out.print(line)
832	            cmd = g.get("cleanup_command", "")
833	            if cmd:
834	                out.print(Text(f"      $ {cmd}", style=f"{color} dim"))
835	            for t in g.get("tasks_highlight", []):
836	                tline = Text()
837	                tline.append("      └ ", style="dim")
838	                tline.append(f"#{t['id']} ", style="bold")
839	                tline.append(f"{t.get('status', '')}", style="yellow")
840	                tline.append(f"  {t.get('summary', '')}", style="white")
841	                out.print(tline)
842	                hint = t.get("recovery_hint", "")
843	                if hint:
844	                    out.print(Text(f"          → {hint}", style="dim italic"))
845	                rcmd = t.get("recovery_command", "")
846	                if rcmd:
847	                    out.print(Text(f"          $ {rcmd}", style="cyan dim"))
848	        out.print()
849

851	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
852	# AI report (markdown)
853	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
854	def render_report(parsed: dict, snapshots: list[HostSnapshot]) -> str:
855	    lines: list[str] = []
856	    ts = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
857	    lines.append(f"# Pueue Report — {ts}")
858	    lines.append("")
859	    fleet = parsed.get("fleet_summary") or ""
860	    if fleet:
861	        lines.append(f"**Fleet:** {fleet}")
862	        lines.append("")
863	
864	    lines.append("## Summary")
865	    lines.append("")
866	    for h in parsed.get("hosts", []):
867	        lines.append(f"- **{h.get('host', '?')}** (daemon: {h.get('daemon', '?')}) — {h.get('overall_summary', '')}")
868	    lines.append("")
869	
870	    lines.append("## Cleanup Candidates")
871	    lines.append("")
872	    any_clean = False
873	    for h in parsed.get("hosts", []):
874	        for g in h.get("groups", []):
875	            if g.get("cleanability") == "safe-to-clean" and g.get("cleanup_command"):
876	                any_clean = True
877	                lines.append(f"- `{h.get('host', '?')}` / `{g.get('name', '?')}` — {g.get('cleanability_reason', '')}")
878	                lines.append(f"  ```bash")
879	                lines.append(f"  {g['cleanup_command']}")
880	                lines.append(f"  ```")
881	    if not any_clean:
882	        lines.append("_None — nothing safely cleanable right now._")
883	    lines.append("")
884	
885	    lines.append("## Failures Needing Action")
886	    lines.append("")
887	    any_fail = False
888	    for h in parsed.get("hosts", []):
889	        for g in h.get("groups", []):
890	            for t in g.get("tasks_highlight", []):
891	                status = t.get("status", "")
892	                if status in ("Failed", "Killed") or t.get("recovery_hint"):
893	                    any_fail = True
894	                    lines.append(f"- `{h.get('host', '?')}` / `{g.get('name', '?')}` / **#{t['id']}** ({status}) — {t.get('summary', '')}")
895	                    hint = t.get("recovery_hint", "")
896	                    if hint:
897	                        lines.append(f"  - Hint: {hint}")
898	                    rcmd = t.get("recovery_command", "")
899	                    if rcmd:
900	                        lines.append(f"  - ```bash")
901	                        lines.append(f"    {rcmd}")
902	                        lines.append(f"    ```")
903	    if not any_fail:
904	        lines.append("_None — all failures (if any) already covered or none present._")
905	    lines.append("")
906	
907	    lines.append("## Raw status")
908	    lines.append("")
909	    lines.append("<details>")
910	    lines.append("<summary>per-host group breakdown</summary>")
911	    lines.append("")
912	    for snap in snapshots:
913	        lines.append(f"### {snap.host}")
914	        lines.append("")
915	        lines.append("| group | daemon | parallel | total | done | progress | eta | statuses |")
916	        lines.append("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
917	        for g in snap.groups:
918	            lines.append(
919	                f"| {g.name} | {g.daemon_status} | {g.parallel_tasks} | {g.total} | {g.done} | "
920	                f"{_fmt_pct(g.pct)} | {_fmt_duration(g.eta_s)} | {_breakdown_str(g.status_breakdown)} |"
921	            )
922	        lines.append("")
923	    lines.append("</details>")
924	    lines.append("")
925	    return "\n".join(lines)
926	
927	
928	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
929	# Execute cleanup
930	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
931	def execute_cleanup(parsed: dict, yes: bool) -> int:
932	    candidates: list[tuple[str, str, str, str]] = []
933	    for h in parsed.get("hosts", []):
934	        host = h.get("host", "?")
935	        for g in h.get("groups", []):
936	            if g.get("cleanability") == "safe-to-clean":
937	                cmd = g.get("cleanup_command", "").strip()
938	                if cmd:
939	                    candidates.append((host, g.get("name", "?"), g.get("cleanability_reason", ""), cmd))
940	    if not candidates:
941	        err.print("[dim]pqsum: nothing safely cleanable right now.[/dim]")
942	        return 0
943	    rc = 0
944	    for host, gname, reason, cmd in candidates:
945	        err.print(f"[bold]{host}[/bold] / [bold]{gname}[/bold] — {reason}")
946	        err.print(f"  [dim]$ {cmd}[/dim]")
947	        if not yes:
948	            try:
949	                answer = input("  run? [y/N] ").strip().lower()
950	            except EOFError:
951	                answer = "n"
952	            if answer not in ("y", "yes"):
953	                err.print("  [dim]skipped[/dim]")
954	                continue
955	        try:
956	            result = subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, check=False, text=True)
957	            if result.returncode != 0:
958	                err.print(f"  [red]exit {result.returncode}[/red]")
959	                rc = max(rc, result.returncode)
960	        except OSError as e:
961	            err.print(f"  [red]failed: {e}[/red]")
962	            rc = max(rc, 1)
963	    return rc
964	
965	
966	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
967	# CLI
968	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
969	def _load_snapshots(stdin_json: bool, raw_stdin: bool, host_override: str, requested_group: str) -> list[HostSnapshot]:
970	    if stdin_json:
971	        raw = sys.stdin.read()
972	        try:
973	            data = json.loads(raw)
974	        except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
975	            err.print(f"[red]pqsum: invalid stdin JSON: {e}[/red]")
976	            sys.exit(2)
977	        if not isinstance(data, list):
978	            err.print("[red]pqsum: --stdin-json expects a JSON array of host snapshots[/red]")
979	            sys.exit(2)
980	        out: list[HostSnapshot] = []
981	        for item in data:
982	            if not isinstance(item, dict):
983	                continue
984	            try:
985	                groups = [GroupRec(**g) for g in item.get("groups", [])]
986	                tasks = [TaskRec(**t) for t in item.get("tasks", [])]
987	            except TypeError as e:
988	                err.print(f"[red]pqsum: stdin host record missing fields: {e}[/red]")
989	                sys.exit(2)
990	            snap_kwargs = {k: v for k, v in item.items() if k not in ("groups", "tasks")}
991	            out.append(HostSnapshot(groups=groups, tasks=tasks, **snap_kwargs))
992	        return out
993	
994	    if raw_stdin:
995	        raw = sys.stdin.read()
996	        try:
997	            snap = parse_pueue_json(raw, requested_group=requested_group)
998	        except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, ValueError) as e:
999	            err.print(f"[red]pqsum: failed to parse raw stdin pueue JSON: {e}[/red]")
1000	            sys.exit(1)
1001	        if host_override:
1002	            snap.host = host_override
1003	        return [snap]
1004	
1005	    if not shutil.which("pueue"):
1006	        err.print("[red]pqsum: pueue not found in PATH[/red]")
1007	        sys.exit(127)
1008	    try:
1009	        result = subprocess.run(["pueue", "status", "--json"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
1010	    except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as e:
1011	        err.print(f"[red]pqsum: failed to run pueue status: {e}[/red]")
1012	        sys.exit(1)
1013	    if result.returncode != 0:
1014	        err.print(f"[red]pqsum: pueue status exited {result.returncode}[/red]")
1015	        if result.stderr.strip():
1016	            err.print(f"[dim]{result.stderr.strip()[:500]}[/dim]")
1017	        sys.exit(result.returncode)
1018	    try:
1019	        return [parse_pueue_json(result.stdout, requested_group=requested_group)]
1020	    except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, ValueError) as e:
1021	        err.print(f"[red]pqsum: failed to parse pueue JSON: {e}[/red]")
1022	        sys.exit(1)
1023	
1024	
1025	def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
1026	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="pqsum", description="pueue queue summary (text + AI + cleanup verdicts).")
1027	    p.add_argument("mode", nargs="?", default="text", choices=["text", "ai", "json"])
1028	    p.add_argument("-g", "--group", default="", help="Restrict to one pueue group.")
1029	    p.add_argument("--stdin-json", action="store_true", help="Read pre-merged host snapshots from stdin (used by `fleet pueue`).")
1030	    p.add_argument("--raw-stdin", action="store_true", help="Read raw `pueue status --json` from stdin (parse one host, used by `fleet pueue` per-host).")
1031	    p.add_argument("--host", default="", help="Override host name when --raw-stdin is set (default: local hostname).")
1032	    p.add_argument("--multi-host", action="store_true", help="Tell the LLM the input is cross-host.")
1033	    p.add_argument("--report", action="store_true", help="Emit markdown report (ai mode only).")
1034	    p.add_argument("--out", default="", help="Write report to PATH (default: stdout).")
1035	    p.add_argument("--clean", action="store_true", help="After AI report, execute cleanup commands on safe-to-clean groups.")
1036	    p.add_argument("--yes", action="store_true", help="Skip y/N prompts for --clean.")
1037	    p.add_argument("--deep", action="store_true", help="Include extra recovery context in prompt.")
1038	    p.add_argument("-r", "--refresh", action="store_true", help="Bypass cache.")
1039	    p.add_argument("--no-cache", action="store_true", help="Don't read or write the cache.")
1040	    p.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="Print AI prompt; no AI call.")
1041	    return p.parse_args()
1042	
1043	
1044	def main() -> int:
1045	    args = parse_args()
1046	    snapshots = _load_snapshots(args.stdin_json, args.raw_stdin, args.host, args.group)
1047

17	Subcommands:

19	  tv [...]                       Launch `tv mlflow` (the fuzzy picker channel)
20	  open <id>                      Open the experiment / run / model page in browser
21	  copy <id>                      Copy an id to the clipboard
22	  plot <run_id> [metric...]      Terminal line plot of metric history (scripts/mlf/plot.py)

24	  download <name>[@version|alias] Download a registered model's artifacts (scripts/mlf/download.py)
25	
26	Backend is read from $MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI (file:./mlruns | sqlite:///path | http(s)://host:port).
27	`open` requires an http(s):// URI; other subcommands work against all three.

29	Mirrors the structure of `fleet` (see dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet).

1	# Zsh & Bash Completions
2	
3	How tab completions are organized in this dotfiles project — for both upstream tools and in-house CLIs (`fleet`, `mlf`, `pqsum`, `mi-router`, `x`).
4	
5	## How autocomplete works (mechanics)
6	
7	Tab completion is the same idea on both shells but the plumbing differs.
8	
9	### zsh — `compinit` + `fpath` + autoload `_<tool>` functions
10	
11	1. **`compinit`** scans every directory in `$fpath` for files starting with `_` and registers them as completion candidates. Run by oh-my-zsh once at startup.
12	2. **`$fpath`** is zsh's function search path. Order in this repo (`dot_zshrc.tmpl:67-70`):
13	   ```
14	   ~/.zfunc                                             ← user-generated (this repo's lazy autoload target)
15	   ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-completions/src/     ← community (184 tools)
16	   ~/.docker/completions/                               ← Docker-shipped
17	   $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/           ← Homebrew-managed
18	   ```
19	3. **The first line of each file** matters: `#compdef <name>` tells zsh which command to bind to. If you write `#compdef fleet`, then `fleet<TAB>` invokes the file's `_fleet` function.
20	4. **Autoload vs eager-load**: a file in `$fpath` is *parsed* the first time the user actually TABs the command (lazy). Files sourced explicitly at startup (e.g. via `load_modular_dir` in this repo) call `compdef _<func> <cmd>` directly — parsed eagerly, no need to be in `$fpath`.
21	5. **`_arguments` DSL** (zsh-only) lets you describe options + positional args declaratively: `'--hosts=[help text]:hosts:_fleet_hosts_csv'` defines the flag, hint, and a custom completer function. See `dot_config/zsh/tools/45_fleet_completion.zsh`.
22	
23	### bash — `bash-completion v2` + `complete -F` + `COMPREPLY`
24	
25	1. **bash-completion v2** is sourced at shell startup by `dot_config/bash/03_completion.bash`. It auto-loads completion files on first TAB.
26	2. **The user dir** is `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions/` — drop a file named after the command (e.g. `mi-router`) here and v2 lazy-loads it on TAB.
27	3. **`complete -F _func cmd`** registers a bash function as the completer for `cmd`. The function reads `$COMP_WORDS` / `$COMP_CWORD` and writes candidates to `$COMPREPLY`.
28	4. **`_init_completion` + `compgen`** are bash-completion v2 helpers — `_init_completion` populates `cur`/`prev`/`words`/`cword`; `compgen -W "list" -- "$cur"` filters a wordlist by the current prefix.
29	5. **Eager vs lazy** mirrors zsh: a file in the user dir is lazy; a file sourced via `load_modular_dir` (this repo's `dot_config/bash/`) calls `complete -F` immediately.
30	
31	### Three generation strategies in this repo
32	
33	| Strategy | Where the file lives | Trigger | Best for |
34	|---|---|---|---|
35	| **A. Lazy autoload** | zsh `~/.zfunc/_<tool>` / bash `${XDG_DATA_HOME}/bash-completion/completions/<tool>` | First TAB on the command | Tools that ship `--print-completion <shell>` or similar (tyro, click, clap-derive — including this repo's `mi-router`) |
36	| **B. Eager-load at startup** | `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<tool>_completion.zsh` + `dot_config/bash/<NN>_<tool>_completion.bash` | Sourced via `load_modular_dir` after compinit / bash-completion v2 init | Hand-written completion (this repo's `fleet`, `mlf`, `pqsum`, `x`) |
37	| **C. Cached eval at startup** | `${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/<shell>/<tool>_completion.<ext>` | Sourced via shell `init` script (`dot_config/shell/<NN>_<tool>.sh`) | Slow generators whose output has side effects beyond `compdef` (e.g. `thefuck --alias` outputs an `alias` line — needs to land in the running shell's namespace, not just a deferred `_<tool>` function) |
38	
39	Cache invalidation in classes A and C uses **binary-mtime check**:
40	```sh
41	[ ! -f "$cache" ] || [ "$(command -v <tool>)" -nt "$cache" ]  # → regenerate
42	```
43	This catches `brew upgrade`, `uv tool upgrade`, `mise install <NEW>` — anything that bumps the binary's mtime. Manual `<tool>-update-completion` helpers (in `dot_config/{shell,zsh}/10_aliases.zsh`) cover edge cases (gem-only upgrades, in-place replacements, cache corruption).
44	
45	## Architecture
46	
47	```
48	compinit runs once (inside oh-my-zsh.sh)
49	        │
50	        ├── ~/.zfunc/                          ← user-generated completions (NOT tracked by chezmoi)
51	        ├── ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/       ← community completions (184 files, cloned by ansible)
52	        │     └── zsh-completions/src/
53	        ├── ~/.docker/completions/             ← Docker-shipped completions
54	        ├── $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/        ← Homebrew-managed completions (via `brew completions link`)
55	        │     └── site-functions/
56	        └── $ZSH/completions/                  ← oh-my-zsh built-in completions
57	```

59	All `fpath` additions are in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` **before** `source "$ZSH/oh-my-zsh.sh"`, so `compinit` runs exactly once and picks up everything.

Manual refresh helpers handle edge cases: gem-only upgrades that don't bump the ruby binary, in-place tool replacements, or cache corruption. 155	
156	- `fleet` host names — `_fleet_hosts_one` / `_fleet_hosts_csv` shell out to `fleet hosts --list`. Used for the positional `fleet hosts NAME`, `fleet chezmoi diff HOST`, `fleet chezmoi tail HOST`, and the `--hosts=foo,bar,baz` CSV flag everywhere.

160	**Adding a new in-house CLI** (decision flow):
161	
162	1. **Does it use tyro?** → Use Strategy A. Mirror `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh`. Add a `<tool>-update-completion` helper to `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh`. Don't forget to rewrite `#compdef` in zsh post-gen.
163	2. **Does it use argparse?** → Two sub-options:
164	   - Add `argcomplete.autocomplete(parser)` to the script + Strategy C cached eval at startup.
165	   - Hand-write Strategy B completion (smaller / no Python dependency at every shell startup).

168	
169	## Why `~/.zfunc/` is NOT Tracked by Chezmoi
170	
171	**Decision: `~/.zfunc/` is not version-controlled.** Rationale:
172	
173	1. **Completions are tool-version-dependent.** A completion script generated by `uv 0.6` may not match `uv 0.7`. Tracking stale files causes subtle breakage.
174	2. **Not all users install the same tools.** A `_pueue` completion file is useless (and throws warnings) if pueue isn't installed.
175	3. **Regeneration is trivial.** One command per tool.
176	4. **Brew-installed tools auto-manage their completions** via site-functions. Duplicating them in `~/.zfunc/` creates conflicts.
177	
178	### What we DO track
179	
180	- `fpath+=~/.zfunc` in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` (ensures the directory is in the search path)
181	- `zsh-completions` plugin cloned by ansible (community completions)
182	- `~/.docker/completions` fpath entry
183	- Tool-specific `eval`/`source` integrations in `dot_config/zsh/tools/`
184	
185	## Generating Completions After Fresh Install
186	
187	**Automatic — no manual step needed.** Every `chezmoi apply` runs `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_50_generate_completions.sh.tmpl`, which calls `scripts/generate_completions.sh` and regenerates completion for the 14 self-generating tools listed in Section A (`chezmoi`, `mise`, `uv`, `just`, `starship`, `gh`, `docker`, `rg`, `fd`, `bat`, `delta`, `zellij`, `pueue`, `opencode`).
188	
189	The hook is **idempotent** — it stat-checks each tool's binary mtime against the existing completion file and skips if the cache is fresh. Cost when nothing changed: **~21ms** total (presence checks + 28 stat calls). After an `ansible-playbook` / `brew upgrade` / `mise install <NEW>` that bumps a binary's mtime: ~140ms one-shot to regenerate the affected completions.
190	
191	Output paths:
192	- **zsh**: `~/.zfunc/_<tool>` — lazy-loaded by compinit on first TAB (in `$fpath` via `dot_zshrc.tmpl:68`).
193	- **bash**: `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions/<tool>` — lazy-loaded by bash-completion v2 on first TAB.
194	
195	### Manual rerun
196	
197	```bash
198	just completions-refresh                              # force regen all (--force)
199	bash scripts/generate_completions.sh --force          # same, no `just`
200	bash scripts/generate_completions.sh                  # mtime-checked (same as the chezmoi hook)
201	```
202	
203	Use `just completions-refresh` after a tool upgrade outside the chezmoi flow (e.g. `cargo install <tool>`), or to recover from a corrupted completion file.
204	
205	### Opt out
206	
207	```bash
208	export CHEZMOI_SKIP_COMPLETION_GEN=1   # in ~/.shellrc.adhoc; suppresses the chezmoi-apply hook
209	```
210	
211	Existing completion files stay as-is; you can still run `just completions-refresh` manually.
212	
213	### Add a new tool to the auto-gen inventory
214	
215	Edit the `regen <tool> "<zsh-args>" "<bash-args>"` block in `scripts/generate_completions.sh`. The arguments are whatever follows the tool name to produce the per-shell completion script — check `<tool> completion --help` or `<tool> --help | grep -i complet`. Examples already in the script cover click (`_TOOL_COMPLETE=`), clap (`--generate complete-<shell>`), tyro (`--tyro-write-completion <shell>`-equivalent), cobra (`completion <shell>`), and ad-hoc styles (`--completions <shell>`).
216	
217	### What about tools NOT in the auto-gen inventory?
218	
219	- **`sesh` / `tv` / `worktrunk`**: shell-startup mtime check (each tool has its own `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<tool>.zsh` file that runs the version check on every shell start — these tools are typically `cargo install`-ed outside chezmoi, so they need the per-startup probe to catch user upgrades).
220	- **`bw` / `marimo` / `thefuck` / `try-cli`**: cached eval at startup (their completion script has side effects beyond `compdef`, so the file is `source`'d into the running shell rather than autoloaded).
221	- **`mi-router`**: tyro self-gen, lives in `dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh` (not the bulk script — has its own `#compdef` rewrite for tyro's full-path output quirk).
222	- **`fleet` / `mlf` / `pqsum` / `x` / `dotcfg`**: hand-written completion in `dot_config/{zsh/tools,bash}/45-51_*_completion.*` (in-house CLIs without a built-in completion generator). `dotcfg`'s `--set` key list mirrors the PROMPTS table in `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py`.
223	
224	## Priority / Override Order
225	
226	When the same `_tool` file exists in multiple fpath directories, the **first match wins**:
227	
228	```
229	1. ~/.zfunc/                                    (highest - your overrides)
230	2. ~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-completions/src/
231	3. ~/.docker/completions/
232	4. $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/   (Homebrew-managed)
233	5. /usr/share/zsh/*/functions/                  (system, lowest)
234	```
235	
236	Current `dot_zshrc.tmpl` order:
237	
238	```zsh
239	fpath+=~/.zfunc                     # appended (lowest of custom)
240	fpath=(zsh-completions/src $fpath)  # prepended (higher than ~/.zfunc)
241	fpath=(~/.docker/completions $fpath) # prepended (highest of custom)
242	```
243	
244	If you want `~/.zfunc/` to override community completions, change to prepend:
245	
246	```zsh
247	fpath=(~/.zfunc $fpath)  # prepend instead of append
248	```
249	
250	## FAQ
251	
252	**Q: Should I generate completions for tools that `zsh-completions` already covers?**
253	A: Only if you want the latest version. The community plugin may lag behind. For fast-moving tools (uv, mise), generating your own is worthwhile.
254	
255	**Q: A completion file throws errors after I uninstall a tool. What do I do?**
256	A: Remove the file: `rm ~/.zfunc/_toolname`. Stale `_tool` files in fpath are harmless (silently ignored) unless they have syntax errors.
257	
258	**Q: How do I debug completion issues?**
259	A: Run `echo $fpath | tr ' ' '\n'` to see all fpath entries. Use `which _toolname` to see which completion file is being used. Force rebuild with `rm -f ~/.zcompdump && compinit`.
260
```

15	2. avoid loading a large project context;

17	4. leave a visible audit trail so the user knows whether the warmup fired.
18	
19	This is not the same as `agent-continue-at`:
20	
21	- no existing tmux pane or blocked agent session is required;
22	- the prompt should not continue real work;
23	- the safest default is a fresh non-interactive run in an isolated directory;
24	- failures should notify/report, not type into a live coding pane.

34	```
35	
36	This uses Claude Code's first-party scheduler (`/loop` / cron-style scheduled
37	tasks) and keeps behavior inside Claude Code. It is low maintenance, but it is
38	session-scoped and depends on Claude Code still running and idle when the task
39	fires.
40	
41	### macOS launchd
42	
43	For a daily local warmup, a user LaunchAgent is a better fit than tmux:
44	
45	```bash
46	mkdir -p ~/.cache/agent-warmup
47	cd ~/.cache/agent-warmup
48	claude -p 'Reply exactly: hi'
49	```
50	
51	Use an isolated cwd like `~/.cache/agent-warmup` so the run does not read a
52	large repo's `CLAUDE.md`, recent files, or tool context. Log stdout/stderr to
53	`~/.cache/agent-warmup/` and treat non-zero exit as a notification-worthy
54	failure.
55	
56	### pueue one-shot wrapper
57	
58	For ad-hoc "tomorrow at 06:00" tasks, a wrapper can submit a delayed pueue job
59	instead of installing a persistent LaunchAgent. This fits the existing local
60	tooling model and gives `pueue status` / future dashboard visibility.
61	
62	The open design question is whether `agent-quota-warmup-at` should use pueue
63	directly for one-shot delays and generate launchd/systemd timers only for
64	recurring schedules.
65	
66	### tmux send-keys
67	
68	Typing into an existing tmux pane can technically start activity, but it is the
69	wrong default for warmup. It risks consuming project/session context and may
70	continue real work accidentally. Reserve pane typing for actual
71	`agent-continue-at` / quota-recovery flows.
72	
73	## Candidate v1
74	
75	Add a shell function or small CLI:
76	
77	```bash
78	agent-quota-warmup-at --agent claude --at 06:00
79	agent-quota-warmup-at --agent claude --at tomorrow-06:00 --prompt 'Reply exactly: hi'
80	agent-quota-warmup-at --agent claude --daily weekdays --time 06:00 --verify-reset
81	agent-quota-warmup-status
82	```
83	
84	Defaults:
85	
86	- `--agent claude` only at first; Codex/OpenCode have different quota systems
87	  and should not be modeled as Claude warmups.
88	- cwd = `~/.cache/agent-warmup/claude`.
89	- prompt = `Reply exactly: hi`.
90	- command = `claude -p "$prompt"` unless testing shows a better low-context
91	  Claude Code invocation.
92	- label/log prefix = `agent-warmup:claude:<timestamp>`.
93	- do not target tmux panes unless `--pane` is explicit.
94	
95	Possible backends:
96	
97	- one-shot: pueue `--delay` job;
98	- daily/weekly on macOS: launchd `StartCalendarInterval`;
99	- daily/weekly on Linux: systemd user timer;
100	- future native TUI: own timer model in `agent-session`.
101	
102	## Verification
103	
104	Do not rely only on the Claude HUD status line. The HUD usage line can be
105	stale; see
106	[claude-hud-usage-statusline-stale.md](../pitfalls/claude-hud-usage-statusline-stale.md).
107	
108	Warmup verification should prefer one or more of:
109	
110	- command exit code and output log;
111	- a fresh usage/reset timestamp from a reliable CLI/status source, if exposed;
112	- timestamped record that a warmup attempt was made;
113	- optional notification when the observed reset time changes.
114	
115	Open empirical check: confirm whether a minimal `claude -p` run starts the same
116	five-hour Claude subscription window as interactive Claude Code usage on the
117	current plan. Do not assume Anthropic API calls count toward the same window;
118	this feature is specifically for Claude Code / Claude subscription usage.
119	
120	## Risks
121	
122	- If the scheduler runs in a large project cwd, "hi" may still consume
123	  project-level context.
124	- If auth expires overnight, warmup silently fails unless logs/notifications are
125	  surfaced.
126	- If the machine is asleep, local launchd/pueue will not fire until wake, so
127	  daily warmup may miss the intended reset geometry.
128	- If provider quota semantics change, a warmup may no longer move the window.
129	
130	## References
131	
132	- Claude Code scheduled tasks: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks
133	- Claude Code Desktop scheduled tasks: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-scheduled-tasks
134	- Claude Code CLI reference: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/cli-reference
135	- Claude Code Pro/Max usage: https://support.anthropic.com/en/articles/11145838-using-claude-code-with-your-pro-or-max-plan
136
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# 48_pqsum_completion.zsh - tab completion for `pqsum` (pueue queue summary).
2	# Source CLI: dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_pqsum (argparse, positional mode +
3	# many flags). Dynamic group completion via `pueue status --json | jq`.
4	
5	(( $+commands[pqsum] )) || return 0
6	
7	_pqsum() {
8	    local context state state_descr line
9	    typeset -A opt_args
10	
11	    _arguments -C \
12	        '(- *)'{-h,--help}'[show help]' \
13	        '(-g --group)'{-g,--group}'=[restrict to one pueue group]:group:->group' \
14	        '--report[emit markdown report (ai mode only)]' \
15	        '--out=[write report to PATH]:path:_files' \
16	        '--clean[execute cleanup commands on safe-to-clean groups]' \
17	        '--yes[skip y/N prompts (with --clean)]' \
18	        '--multi-host[tell LLM the input describes multiple hosts]' \
19	        '--stdin-json[read pre-merged host snapshots from stdin]' \
20	        '--raw-stdin[read raw `pueue status --json` from stdin]' \
21	        '--host=[override host name when --raw-stdin is set]:hostname:_hosts' \
22	        '--deep[include extra recovery context (last ~20 log lines per failed task)]' \
23	        '(-r --refresh)'{-r,--refresh}'[bypass prompt-hash cache]' \
24	        '--no-cache[do not read or write the cache]' \
25	        '--dry-run[print AI prompt; no AI call]' \
26	        '1:mode:(text ai json)'
27	
28	    case "$state" in
29	        group)
30	            local -a groups
31	            if (( $+commands[pueue] )) && (( $+commands[jq] )); then
32	                groups=( ${(f)"$(pueue status --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.groups | keys[]' 2>/dev/null)"} )
33	                (( ${#groups} )) && _describe 'pueue group' groups
34	            fi
35	            ;;
36	    esac
37	}
38	
39	compdef _pqsum pqsum
40
```

1	# 45_fleet_completion.zsh - tab completion for `fleet` (fleet-apply umbrella).
2	# Source CLI: dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet (hand-rolled dispatcher) +
3	# scripts/fleet/{apply,tmux,info,pueue,exec,hosts}.py (tyro + argparse mix).
4	# Dynamic host names via `fleet hosts --list`.
5	#
6	# Layout per the umbrella USAGE string:
7	#   fleet chezmoi {apply,status,diff,tail,kill,compact} [...]
8	#   fleet {edit,tmux,info,pueue,exec,hosts} [...]
9	
10	(( $+commands[fleet] )) || return 0
11	
12	# Dynamic helpers ------------------------------------------------------------
13	
14	_fleet_hosts_one() {
15	    local -a hosts
16	    hosts=( ${(f)"$(fleet hosts --list 2>/dev/null)"} )
17	    (( ${#hosts} )) && _describe -t hosts 'fleet host' hosts
18	}
19	
20	_fleet_hosts_csv() {
21	    local -a hosts
22	    hosts=( ${(f)"$(fleet hosts --list 2>/dev/null)"} )
23	    (( ${#hosts} )) && _values -s , 'fleet host' $hosts
24	}
25	
26	# Subcommand completions -----------------------------------------------------
27	
28	_fleet_chezmoi_apply() {
29	    _arguments \
30	        '--hosts=[comma-separated host names]:hosts:_fleet_hosts_csv' \
31	        '--dry-run[show what would change without applying]' \
32	        '--force[overwrite remote drift]' \
33	        '--serial[run hosts sequentially]' \
34	        '--branch=[git branch to apply (no-op on local hosts)]:branch:' \
35	        '--readiness[pre-flight readiness probe]' \
36	        '--readiness-no-fetch[skip remote git fetch]' \
37	        '--readiness-json[JSON output for readiness]' \
38	        '--status[process-liveness probe]' \
39	        '--watch=[poll every N seconds (with --status)]:seconds:'
40	}
41	
42	_fleet_chezmoi_status() {
43	    _arguments \
44	        '--quick[skip remote git fetch (faster)]' \
45	        '--live[process-liveness probe (use during/after apply)]' \
46	        '--watch=[poll every N seconds (with --live)]:seconds:'
47	}
48	
49	_fleet_chezmoi() {
50	    local context state state_descr line
51	    typeset -A opt_args
52	
53	    _arguments -C \
54	        '1: :->action' \
55	        '*::action_arg:->action_args'
56	
57	    case "$state" in
58	        action)
59	            local -a actions=(
60	                'apply:Run chezmoi update --init across the fleet'
61	                'status:Pre-flight readiness probe (--quick / --live for variants)'
62	                'diff:chezmoi diff on one host (--dry-run --hosts HOST --serial)'
63	                'tail:Live-tail a remote fleet-apply log (positional HOST[:RUN_ID])'
64	                'kill:pkill chezmoi/ansible across the fleet'
65	                'compact:Post-mortem summary'
66	            )
67	            _describe -t chezmoi-actions 'fleet chezmoi action' actions
68	            ;;
69	        action_args)
70	            case "$line[1]" in
71	                apply)   _fleet_chezmoi_apply ;;
72	                status)  _fleet_chezmoi_status ;;
73	                diff|tail) _fleet_hosts_one ;;
74	                kill)    _arguments '--hosts=[comma-separated host names]:hosts:_fleet_hosts_csv' ;;
75	                compact) _arguments '--run-id=[specific apply run id]:run-id:' ;;
76	            esac
77	            ;;
78	    esac
79	}
80	
81	_fleet_tmux() {
82	    _arguments \
83	        '--hosts=[comma-separated host names]:hosts:_fleet_hosts_csv' \
84	        '--json[emit JSON]' \
85	        '--deep[include visible pane area (slower)]'
86	}
87	
88	_fleet_info() {
89	    _arguments \
90	        '--hosts=[comma-separated host names]:hosts:_fleet_hosts_csv' \
91	        '--ff[fast-fail mode]' \
92	        '--full[full report]' \
93	        '--modules=[comma-separated module names]:modules:' \
94	        '--json[emit JSON]'
95	}
96	
97	_fleet_pueue() {
98	    _arguments \
99	        '--hosts=[comma-separated host names]:hosts:_fleet_hosts_csv' \
100	        '--group=[restrict to one pueue group]:group:' \
101	        '--json[emit JSON]' \
102	        '--ai[AI summary via pqsum]' \
103	        '--report[markdown report (with --ai)]' \
104	        '--out=[write report to PATH]:path:_files'
105	}
106	
107	_fleet_exec() {
108	    _arguments \
109	        '--hosts=[comma-separated host names]:hosts:_fleet_hosts_csv' \
110	        '--shell=[opt-in shell expansion]:shell:(bash zsh sh)' \
111	        '--login[full rc-loaded env]' \
112	        '--json[emit JSON]' \
113	        '--out-dir=[write per-host output to DIR]:dir:_directories' \
114	        '--ai[succeeded/differed/failed classification]' \
115	        '*::cmd: _normal'
116	}
117	
118	_fleet_hosts() {
119	    _arguments \
120	        '--list[plain host names, one per line]' \
121	        '--list-tsv[TSV name<TAB>target<TAB>kind (used by tv cable source)]' \
122	        '--list-json[full inventory as JSON]' \
123	        '--describe=[print preview block for NAME]:host:_fleet_hosts_one' \
124	        '--probe=[BatchMode SSH probe of NAME]:host:_fleet_hosts_one' \
125	        '--include-local[include local hosts in --list-tsv]' \
126	        '--config=[fleet inventory path]:path:_files' \
127	        ':host:_fleet_hosts_one'
128	}
129	
130	# Top-level dispatcher -------------------------------------------------------
131	
132	_fleet() {
133	    local context state state_descr line
134	    typeset -A opt_args
135	
136	    _arguments -C \
137	        '1: :->subcommand' \
138	        '*::arg:->args'
139	
140	    case "$state" in
141	        subcommand)
142	            local -a subs=(
143	                'chezmoi:Chezmoi-specific deploy ops (apply/status/diff/tail/kill/compact)'
144	                'edit:Open ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml in $EDITOR'
145	                'tmux:Cross-host tmux session summary'
146	                'info:Cross-host system status snapshot'
147	                'pueue:Cross-host pueue queue summary'
148	                'exec:Cross-host ad-hoc command runner (use -- to separate CMD)'
149	                'hosts:Pick a fleet-configured host and SSH in (or list inventory)'
150	            )
151	            _describe -t subcommands 'fleet subcommand' subs
152	            ;;
153	        args)
154	            case "$line[1]" in
155	                chezmoi) _fleet_chezmoi ;;
156	                tmux)    _fleet_tmux ;;
157	                info)    _fleet_info ;;
158	                pueue)   _fleet_pueue ;;
159	                exec)    _fleet_exec ;;
160	                hosts)   _fleet_hosts ;;
161	                edit)    ;;  # no args
162	            esac
163	            ;;
164	    esac
165	}
166	
167	compdef _fleet fleet

```text
1	# Agent delayed-run scheduler for non-quota work
2	
3	**Status**: P? research captured (2026-06)
4	**Effort**: M
5	**Related**: `dot_config/television/executable_agent-wakeup.py`, `dot_config/shell/62_agent_wakeup.sh`, [docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md](../docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md), [backlog/agent-quota-auto-loop.md](agent-quota-auto-loop.md), [backlog/agent-quota-warmup-at-time.md](agent-quota-warmup-at-time.md), [backlog/agent-session-dashboard-tui.md](agent-session-dashboard-tui.md)
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	Quota wakeups are only one instance of a broader need: leave an agent session
10	half-finished, then resume it at a known future time. Example: implement a
11	market-data pipeline now, then wait until the stock market opens to run a live
12	smoke test and continue fixing failures.
13	
14	This differs from quota recovery:
15	
16	- quota waits are imposed by the provider and show explicit reset text;
17	- delayed work is user-intentional and may happen while quota is available;
18	- the scheduler needs to remember the target session, cwd, prompt, and whether
19	  to resume an existing conversation or start a fresh run.
20	
21	It also differs from quota warmup, where the goal is to start a provider usage
22	window with a tiny prompt and explicitly avoid continuing real work; see
23	[agent-quota-warmup-at-time.md](agent-quota-warmup-at-time.md).
24	
25	## Investigation
26	
27	### Claude Code
28	
29	Claude Code has first-party scheduling surfaces:
30	
31	- Session-scoped scheduling with `/loop` and cron-style tools. The docs say
32	  scheduled tasks live in the current conversation, require Claude Code
33	  v2.1.72+, can be listed/cancelled via `CronList`/`CronDelete`, and are
34	  restored by `claude --resume` / `claude --continue` if unexpired. They only
35	  fire while Claude Code is running and idle, and background Bash/monitor tasks
36	  are not restored on resume.
37	- Desktop scheduled tasks start new sessions at a selected time/frequency on
38	  the local machine, with local files/tools available while the Desktop app is
39	  open and the machine is awake.
40	- Routines run on Anthropic-managed infrastructure and can keep running even
41	  when the local machine is off, but they do not have direct access to
42	  uncommitted local state.
43	- `/goal` keeps the current session working across turns until a condition is
44	  met; it is useful for "keep going until tests pass", but it is not itself a
45	  wall-clock delayed start.
46	
47	### Codex
48	
49	Codex has first-party Automations in the Codex app:
50	
51	- Standalone automations run fresh scheduled tasks and report findings to the
52	  app inbox.
53	- Thread automations are recurring wake-ups attached to the current thread,
54	  preserving thread context.
55	- Project-scoped local automations require the local Codex app to be running,
56	  the machine powered on, and the selected project still available on disk.
57	- Codex CLI has `codex resume` for interactive sessions and
58	  `codex exec resume [SESSION_ID]` / `codex exec resume --last [PROMPT]` for
59	  non-interactive resumption, but the CLI reference does not expose a native
60	  local `schedule` subcommand.
61	
62	### OpenCode
63	
64	OpenCode core CLI is scriptable but not scheduler-first:
65	
66	- `opencode run` supports non-interactive runs, `--continue`, `--session`,
67	  `--attach`, and `opencode serve`.
68	- OpenCode's GitHub integration supports GitHub Actions `schedule` events for
69	  cron-based runs in CI.
70	- The official ecosystem page lists third-party scheduler/orchestration
71	  projects, including `opencode-scheduler`, but that is not the same as a
72	  core cross-agent local scheduler.
73	
74	## Options considered
75	
76	| Option | Pros | Cons |
77	|---|---|---|
78	| A. Use native scheduling where available | Lowest maintenance; Claude/Codex already know their own session semantics | Surface-specific; not portable across Claude/Codex/OpenCode; may not target an existing tmux pane |
79	| B. Repo wrapper: `agent-run-at` / `agent-resume-at` | One command for "run this prompt at 09:30"; can use pueue labels/status; works for stock-open tests and other one-shot waits | Needs per-agent adapters and careful auth/permission defaults |
80	| C. Extend `agent-wakeup` beyond quota | Reuses current TV + pueue backend and pane discovery | The name/mental model is quota-specific; typing into panes remains fragile |
81	| D. Native dashboard/daemon owns timers | Best long-term state model; unifies quota, delayed work, transcript links, and manual controls | Larger design, overlaps with `agent-session-dashboard-tui.md` |
82	
83	## Current decision
84	
85	`2026-06-19`: document native surfaces and keep a repo backlog item for a
86	cross-agent local wrapper.
87	
88	Use native features first when they fit:
89	
90	- Claude Code `/loop` for quick in-session polling.
91	- Claude Code Desktop scheduled tasks or Routines for durable Claude-only
92	  scheduling.
93	- Codex App Automations for Codex-only recurring or thread wakeups.
94	- OpenCode GitHub scheduled workflows for CI-based tasks.
95	
96	Still worth building a repo-local wrapper when the task is specifically:
97	
98	- tied to a tmux pane or existing terminal session;
99	- cross-agent (`claude`, `codex`, `opencode`, Cursor Agent);
100	- a one-shot future continuation, not a recurring automation;
101	- dependent on uncommitted local state and the user's exact machine/tooling;
102	- something the user wants visible in the same `agent-wakeup` /
103	  future `agent-session` dashboard.
104	
105	## Candidate v1
106	
107	Add `agent-run-at` or extend `agent-continue-at` with an explicit mode:
108	
109	```bash
110	agent-run-at --agent claude --cwd "$PWD" --at 09:31 \
111	  --prompt "Run the live market-open smoke test and fix failures."
112	
113	agent-run-at --agent codex --cwd "$PWD" --delay 2h \
114	  --resume-last --prompt "Continue from the previous plan and run verification."
115	
116	agent-run-at --agent opencode --cwd "$PWD" --at tomorrow-09:30 \
117	  --session <id> --prompt "Run the post-open validation."
118	```
119	
120	Backend:
121	
122	- pueue group `agent-scheduler`, labels like
123	  `agent-scheduler:<agent>:<project>:<time>`;
124	- adapters for command construction:
125	  - Claude: prefer native `/loop`/Desktop for active Claude sessions; external
126	    fallback can launch `claude --continue` or send to a tmux pane.
127	  - Codex: `codex exec resume --last <prompt>` or session-specific resume.
128	  - OpenCode: `opencode run --continue <prompt>` or `--session <id>`.
129	- dashboard rows for scheduled future work independent from quota waits.
130	
131	## Open questions
132	
133	- Should v1 launch non-interactive CLI runs, or type into an existing tmux
134	  pane? Non-interactive is safer; pane typing preserves exact TUI session
135	  context.
136	- How should the wrapper resolve "last session" safely when multiple sessions
137	  share a cwd?
138	- Should scheduled tasks inherit bypass/approval modes, or require explicit
139	  flags per task?
140	- Do we want one queue group for all agent jobs, or separate
141	  `agent-wakeup` and `agent-scheduler` groups?
142	- Can Codex App Automations be controlled from CLI/API enough to avoid a
143	  separate local wrapper for Codex?
144	
145	## References
146	
147	- Claude Code scheduled tasks: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks
148	- Claude Code Desktop scheduled tasks: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-scheduled-tasks
149	- Claude Code `/goal`: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal
150	- Claude Code common workflows: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/common-workflows
151	- Codex Automations: https://developers.openai.com/codex/app/automations
152	- Codex CLI reference: https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/reference
153	- OpenCode CLI: https://opencode.ai/docs/cli/
154	- OpenCode GitHub schedule support: https://opencode.ai/docs/github/
155	- OpenCode ecosystem scheduler entry: https://opencode.ai/docs/ecosystem/
156
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# Agent wakeup reports quota wait from stale Claude HUD usage line
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section): `agent-wakeup status` reports
4	`WAIT_QUOTA` or a future reset time even though Claude Code already accepted
5	`continue`; tmux pane bottom bar still shows `Usage ... Limit reached`; pane
6	shows `Scampering` / active work while the detector says quota-blocked;
7	`Context ... | Usage ... Limit reached (resets ...)` appears in captured pane
8	scrollback.
9	**First seen**: 2026-06-19
10	**Affects**: Claude Code panes using the `claude-hud` statusLine plugin plus
11	tmux capture-based quota detectors
12	**Status**: fixed in `agent-wakeup` by ignoring Claude HUD usage lines
13	
14	## Symptom
15	
16	A Claude Code pane can be working normally after quota reset, while the bottom
17	status area still contains a line like:
18	
19	```text
20	Context ... | Usage ... Limit reached (resets 1h 22m)
21	```
22	
23	If a quota detector scans the last screenful of tmux output for `Limit reached`,
24	it may classify the pane as `WAIT_QUOTA` even though the agent is active and
25	has already accepted `continue`.
26	
27	In the first incident, `vibe/libkdc-simple-demo` accepted a smart
28	`agent-wakeup send-now --auto`, printed `Scampering`, and continued running.
29	The old HUD usage line remained visible long enough for the detector to keep
30	reporting quota wait until the parser was fixed.
31	
32	## Root cause
33	
34	`claude-hud` is a Claude Code `statusLine` command, not a live agent-state
35	protocol. Claude Code launches the plugin for rendering; the plugin reads
36	stdin/transcript/cwd and fetches usage through its own cached API layer.
37	
38	The installed plugin implementation stores usage in:
39	
40	```text
41	~/.claude/plugins/claude-hud/.usage-cache.json
42	```
43	
44	The source in the plugin cache documents that the HUD runs as a new process
45	each render and therefore uses a file-based cache. It also preserves
46	`lastGoodData` during usage API rate-limited periods. That is correct for a
47	human status bar, but it means `Usage ... Limit reached` is not proof that
48	the current pane is blocked on `/rate-limit-options`.
49	
50	## Fix
51	
52	The repo-side detector now strips ANSI and ignores Claude HUD usage lines
53	before applying quota regexes:
54	
55	- `dot_config/television/executable_agent-wakeup.py`
56	- Commit: `4c0bf51f Ignore Claude HUD quota status in wakeup detector`
57	
58	Real quota/menu detection should come from fresh agent output such as:
59	
60	```text
61	You've hit your session limit
62	/rate-limit-options
63	What do you want to do?
64	Stop and wait for limit to reset
65	```
66	
67	Do not treat `Context ... | Usage ... Limit reached` or `Usage ... Limit
68	reached` from the HUD as an authoritative pane state.
69	
70	## Diagnostics
71	
72	```bash
73	# See what the wakeup detector thinks now.
74	agent-wakeup status
75	
76	# Inspect the pane tail directly.
77	tmux capture-pane -p -S -80 -t %39 | tail -n 60
78	
79	# Inspect the HUD usage cache without dumping credentials.
80	jq '{timestamp, data: {planName: .data.planName, fiveHour: .data.fiveHour,
81	    sevenDay: .data.sevenDay, fiveHourResetAt: .data.fiveHourResetAt,
82	    sevenDayResetAt: .data.sevenDayResetAt, apiError: .data.apiError}}' \
83	  ~/.claude/plugins/claude-hud/.usage-cache.json
84	```
85	
86	If the pane is actively thinking/running but only the HUD line mentions
87	`Limit reached`, the pane is not quota-blocked.
88	
89	## Prevention
90	
91	- For tmux capture parsers, separate user-facing status bars from agent
92	  conversation/tool output.
93	- Prefer explicit state markers (`/rate-limit-options`, quota error text,
94	  process/session status files) over broad `limit reached` regexes.
95	- Re-check a pane immediately before sending scheduled input, and abort if the
96	  explicit quota marker is gone.
97	
98	## Related
99	
100	- [docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md](../docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md)
101	- [backlog/agent-quota-auto-loop.md](../backlog/agent-quota-auto-loop.md)
102	- [backlog/agent-session-dashboard-tui.md](../backlog/agent-session-dashboard-tui.md)
103
```
</details></tool-use>

 `./docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md`

```text
1	# Agent pane discovery
2	
3	Find — and jump to — coding-agent sessions (`claude`, `cursor-agent`, `codex`,
4	`opencode`) that are currently running in *any* tmux pane on this host.
5	
6	The pain this solves: you start `claude` in pane A on session `chezmoi`, hop
7	into pane B in another window for a quick test, drift over to a `vibe/foo`
8	session for a Codex task, and three windows later you can't remember which
9	pane has the agent you wanted to nudge. CodeIsland (macOS) tells you which
10	**terminal app** is running an agent, but not the specific tmux pane —
11	useless once you have more than one agent inside one terminal.
12	
13	Two complementary surfaces ship in this repo, both backed by tmux:
14	
15	| Tool | Scope | Best at |
16	|---|---|---|
17	| `tv agent-panes` | All four agents (Claude / Codex / OpenCode / Cursor) | "Where am I running stuff?" cross-agent overview, jump-to-pane |
18	| `tv agent-wakeup` | Same live panes, plus pueue wakeup tasks | "Which agent is quota-blocked, when should I send `continue`?" |
19	| `recon` (optional) | Claude-only, with live status (Working / Idle / Waiting) parsed from pane capture | "Which Claude needs my attention?" — recon's live status detection is richer than what we replicate in tv |
20	
21	## `tv agent-panes` (primary)
22	
23	Open the picker with `prefix + a` inside tmux, or via the popup menu
24	(`prefix + Space → → Agents → Live agent panes (tv)`), or from any shell
25	with `tv agent-panes`.
26	
27	Each row is one running agent pane. The status column shows ● (busy) or
28	○ (idle) for Claude (read from `~/.claude/sessions/{pid}.json`); blank for
29	others.
30	
31	```
32	[cc] ● chezmoi:1.1     │  discover-coding-agent-sessions          │  chezmoi
33	[cc] ○ chezmoi:2.1     │  fix-nvm-lazy-loader-permission-request  │  chezmoi
34	[cc] ●  vibe/foo:4.1   │  refactor auth module                    │  foo
35	[oc]   vibe/bar:0.0    │  Generate migration script               │  bar
36	```
37	
38	### Keybindings (in the picker)
39	
40	| Key | Action |
41	|---|---|
42	| `Enter` / `Alt+T` | Switch tmux focus to that session/window/pane |
43	| `Alt+K` | Kill the pane (with `[y/N]` confirm) |
44	| `Ctrl+Y` | Copy the pane target (`session:win.pane`) to clipboard |
45	| `Alt+P` | Copy directory path |
46	| `Alt+R` | Copy session ID |
47	| `Alt+S` | Copy matched `.specstory/history/*.md` path |
48	| `Ctrl+F` | Cycle preview: live `tmux capture-pane` snapshot ↔ stored transcript |
49	| `Esc` | Close the picker |
50	
51	### How resolution works
52	
53	- **Claude** — Claude Code writes a per-process file at
54	  `~/.claude/sessions/{claude_pid}.json` containing `sessionId`, `cwd`,
55	  `status`, and (when set) a friendly `name`. The discovery walker reads
56	  these directly — *zero heuristics* for Claude. It then walks each
57	  `claude_pid`'s parent chain via `ps -o ppid=` until it finds a tmux
58	  `pane_pid`, which gives the pane target.
59	- **Codex / OpenCode / Cursor** — `pgrep -x <bin>` finds running agent
60	  PIDs, parent-chain walked the same way. Session ID is best-effort: the
61	  walker queries each agent's storage (`opencode.db`, `~/.codex/sessions`,
62	  `~/.cursor/chats`) for the most-recent matching session whose `cwd`
63	  equals the pane's `pane_current_path`. If multiple sessions share a
64	  cwd, the most recently updated wins. The pane is still listed even if
65	  no session ID matches — the row is useful for jump-to-pane regardless.
66	
67	## `tv agent-wakeup` (quota waits + scheduled continue)
68	
69	Open with `prefix + M-a`, via the popup menu
70	(`prefix + Space → → Agents → Quota wakeup (tv)`), or from a shell with
71	`tv agent-wakeup`.
72	
73	The channel reuses the live pane resolver from `tv agent-panes`, captures the
74	last part of each pane scrollback, and conservatively marks panes as quota
75	waiting only when it sees explicit limit wording such as `session limit`,
76	`rate limit`, `limit reached`, or `quota`. It parses reset phrases like
77	`resets 1:50am`, `resets in 70m`, or `resets in 5h 20m`, then shows any
78	queued pueue wakeup task for the pane.
79	
80	Claude HUD usage lines such as `Context ... | Usage Limit reached` are
81	ignored because `claude-hud` renders from cached/API usage data and is not an
82	authoritative live indicator that the pane is currently blocked.
83	
84	`WAIT_MENU` is the Claude `/rate-limit-options` screen where option 1
85	(`Stop and wait for limit to reset`) is already selected. For that state the
86	recommended action is `enter`, not `continue`.
87	
88	| Key | Action |
89	|---|---|
90	| `Enter` | Switch tmux focus to that pane |
91	| `Alt+C` | Schedule a smart wakeup at the detected reset time + 2 minutes |
92	| `Alt+T` | Prompt for a custom time/delay (`01:52am`, `70m`, `5h`, etc.) |
93	| `Alt+N` | Smart send now: `Enter` for `WAIT_MENU`, otherwise `continue` + Enter |
94	| `Alt+X` | Cancel queued wakeup tasks for that pane |
95	| `Ctrl+F` | Cycle preview; the default preview is live `tmux capture-pane` output |
96	
97	The shell equivalent is:
98	
99	```bash
100	agent-wakeup status
101	agent-continue-at --pane %12 --at 01:52am
102	agent-wakeup send-now --pane %44 --auto        # Enter for /rate-limit-options, continue otherwise
103	agent-wakeup send-now --pane %44 --enter-only  # force selecting Stop-and-wait menu item
104	agent-continue-at --current --delay 70m
105	agent-wakeup cancel --pane %12
106	```
107	
108	Scheduled wakeups are pueue tasks in group `agent-wakeup` with labels
109	`agent-wakeup:%pane_id`. The scheduled task re-captures the pane right before
110	sending. If the quota marker has disappeared, it aborts instead of blindly
111	typing into a session that may already be doing unrelated work. With `--auto`,
112	the send step re-captures the pane and chooses `Enter` for a rate-limit menu
113	or `continue` for a normal prompt.
114	
115	The fully automatic "detect quota, schedule, continue, repeat until non-quota
116	exit" supervisor is deliberately deferred; see
117	[`backlog/agent-quota-auto-loop.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/agent-quota-auto-loop.md).
118	
119	## Scheduled work beyond quota waits
120	
121	For non-quota delayed work, prefer native agent scheduling when it fits:
122	
123	- Claude Code has session-scoped `/loop` / cron tasks, Desktop scheduled
124	  tasks, and cloud Routines.
125	- Codex App has Automations, including thread automations that wake up the
126	  same thread on a schedule.
127	- OpenCode is scriptable through `opencode run --continue` / `--session`, and
128	  its GitHub integration supports cron schedules in GitHub Actions.
129	
130	Those native surfaces are better for agent-owned scheduled work. The local
131	`agent-wakeup` / pueue path is still useful when the target is a specific tmux
132	pane, a one-shot future continuation, or a cross-agent workflow that should
133	show up in the same dashboard. The broader local wrapper idea is tracked in
134	[`backlog/agent-delayed-run-scheduler.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/agent-delayed-run-scheduler.md).
135	
136	## `recon` (Claude-only fast popup, optional)
137	
138	[`gavraz/recon`](https://github.com/gavraz/recon) is a Rust TUI dashboard
139	that focuses on Claude Code only but pays attention to live agent status by
140	parsing the Claude TUI status bar via `tmux capture-pane`. Worth keeping
141	around when you're juggling several Claude sessions and want
142	"who's blocked on me?" at a glance.
143	
144	### Install
145	
146	Installed automatically via the `rust_cargo_tools` ansible role on
147	`chezmoi apply`:
148	
149	```bash
150	cargo install --git https://github.com/gavraz/recon --locked
```
</details></tool-use>

81	## Agent wakeups
82	
83	`agent-wakeup` uses pueue as a small persistent scheduler for quota/rate-limit
84	resets in live coding-agent panes. It creates group `agent-wakeup`, sets group
85	parallelism to 1, and labels each task as `agent-wakeup:%pane_id`.
86	
87	```bash
88	agent-wakeup status
89	agent-continue-at --pane %12 --at 01:52am
90	agent-wakeup send-now --pane %44 --auto
91	agent-wakeup send-now --pane %44 --enter-only
92	agent-continue-at --current --delay 70m
93	agent-wakeup cancel --pane %12
94	```
95	
96	The scheduled command calls back into
97	`~/.config/television/agent-wakeup.py send-now`. When the task runs, it
98	captures the target tmux pane again. If the original quota marker has
99	disappeared, the task exits without sending text unless `--force` was used.
100	That guard is intentional: scheduled `continue` should not type into a pane
101	that may already have resumed or changed context.
102	
103	Use `--auto` when you do not know whether the pane needs `continue` or only
104	`Enter`: Claude's `/rate-limit-options` screen is treated as `Enter` because
105	`Stop and wait for limit to reset` is already selected; normal prompts use
106	`continue` + Enter. Use `--enter-only` to force the menu selection.
107	
108	For the dashboard UI, use `tv agent-wakeup` or tmux `prefix + M-a`. See
109	[Agent pane discovery](agent-panes-discovery.md#tv-agent-wakeup-quota-waits--scheduled-continue).
110
```

## Comprehensive Summary of Agent Wakeup / Quota Recovery Tooling

I've thoroughly analyzed the agent wakeup/quota recovery system in your chezmoi dotfiles. Here's the complete breakdown:
