```text
137	_ANSI_RE = re.compile(r"\x1b\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~]")
138	_QUOTA_LINE_RE = re.compile(
139	    r"(session limit|rate limit|limit reached|hit your .*limit|quota)",
140	    re.IGNORECASE,
141	)
142	_RESET_RE = re.compile(r"\bresets?\b(?:\s+in)?\s+([^)\n\r]+)", re.IGNORECASE)
143	_RATE_LIMIT_MENU_RE = re.compile(
144	    r"(/rate-limit-options|stop and wait for limit to reset|what do you want to do\?)",
145	    re.IGNORECASE,
146	)
147	_CLAUDE_HUD_USAGE_RE = re.compile(
148	    r"(^|\s│\s)Usage\s+.*\bLimit reached\b",
149	    re.IGNORECASE,
150	)
151	
152	
153	def _strip_ansi(text: str) -> str:
154	    return _ANSI_RE.sub("", text)
155	
156	
157	def _is_claude_hud_usage_line(line: str) -> bool:
158	    """claude-hud statusLine usage is cached/non-authoritative for wakeups."""
159	    plain = _strip_ansi(line).strip()
160	    if not _CLAUDE_HUD_USAGE_RE.search(plain):
161	        return False
162	    return plain.startswith("Usage ") or plain.startswith("Context ") or " │ Usage " in plain
163	
164	
165	def _format_dt(dt: datetime) -> str:
166	    return dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
167	
168	
169	def _parse_reset_expr(expr: str, now: datetime) -> datetime | None:
170	    expr = expr.strip()
171	    expr = re.split(r"\s*[·|]\s*", expr, maxsplit=1)[0].strip()
172	    expr = re.sub(r"\s*\([^)]*\)\s*$", "", expr).strip()
173	    expr = expr.rstrip(".,; ")
174	
175	    m = re.search(
176	        r"(?:(\d+)\s*h(?:ours?)?)?\s*(?:(\d+)\s*m(?:in(?:ute)?s?)?)",
177	        expr,
178	        re.IGNORECASE,
179	    )
180	    if m and (m.group(1) or m.group(2)):
181	        hours = int(m.group(1) or 0)
182	        mins = int(m.group(2) or 0)
183	        return now + timedelta(hours=hours, minutes=mins)
184	
185	    m = re.search(r"\b(\d+)\s*(?:seconds?|secs?|s)\b", expr, re.IGNORECASE)
186	    if m:
187	        return now + timedelta(seconds=int(m.group(1)))
188	
189	    m = re.search(r"\b(\d+)\s*(?:days?|d)\b", expr, re.IGNORECASE)
190	    if m:
191	        return now + timedelta(days=int(m.group(1)))
192	
193	    time_match = re.search(r"\b(\d{1,2})(?::(\d{2}))?\s*(am|pm)?\b", expr, re.IGNORECASE)
194	    if time_match:
195	        hour = int(time_match.group(1))
196	        minute = int(time_match.group(2) or 0)
197	        ampm = (time_match.group(3) or "").lower()
198	        if ampm == "pm" and hour < 12:
199	            hour += 12
200	        elif ampm == "am" and hour == 12:
201	            hour = 0
202	        if hour > 23 or minute > 59:
203	            return None
204	        dt = now.replace(hour=hour, minute=minute, second=0, microsecond=0)
205	        if dt <= now:
206	            dt += timedelta(days=1)
207	        return dt
208	
209	    return None
210

212	def detect_quota(text: str, now: datetime | None = None) -> tuple[str, int, str]:
213	    now = now or datetime.now().astimezone()
214	    quota_lines = [
215	        line.strip()
216	        for line in text.splitlines()
217	        if _QUOTA_LINE_RE.search(line) and not _is_claude_hud_usage_line(line)
218	    ]
219	    if not quota_lines:
220	        return ("", 0, "")
221	
222	    reset_dt: datetime | None = None
223	    chosen = quota_lines[-1]
224	    for line in reversed(quota_lines):
225	        m = _RESET_RE.search(line)
226	        if not m:
227	            continue
228	        reset_dt = _parse_reset_expr(m.group(1), now)
229	        chosen = line
230	        if reset_dt:
231	            break
232	
233	    if reset_dt:
234	        return (chosen, int(reset_dt.timestamp()), _format_dt(reset_dt))
235	    return (chosen, 0, "")

238	def recommended_action(text: str) -> str:
239	    if _RATE_LIMIT_MENU_RE.search(text):
240	        return ACTION_ENTER
241	    return ACTION_CONTINUE

244	def active_quota_text(text: str, action: str) -> str:
245	    if action == ACTION_ENTER:

250	def _status_name(status: Any) -> str:
251	    if isinstance(status, str):
252	        return status
253	    if isinstance(status, dict) and status:
254	        return next(iter(status.keys()))
255	    return str(status)
256	
257	
258	def _datetime_from_status(task: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
259	    candidates: list[str] = []
260	
261	    def walk(v: Any) -> None:
262	        if isinstance(v, dict):
263	            for key, val in v.items():
264	                if key in {"enqueue_at", "enqueued_at", "start", "created_at"} and isinstance(val, str):
265	                    candidates.append(val)
266	                walk(val)
267	        elif isinstance(v, list):
268	            for item in v:
269	                walk(item)
270	
271	    walk(task.get("status"))
272	    if isinstance(task.get("created_at"), str):
273	        candidates.append(str(task["created_at"]))
274	    for value in candidates:
275	        try:
276	            return _format_dt(datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace("Z", "+00:00")).astimezone())
277	        except ValueError:
278	            continue
279	    return ""

282	def _pueue_tasks() -> list[WakeTask]:
283	    if not shutil.which("pueue"):
284	        return []
285	    cp = run(["pueue", "status", "--json"])
286	    if cp.returncode != 0:
287	        return []
288	    try:
289	        data = json.loads(cp.stdout)
290	    except json.JSONDecodeError:
291	        return []
292	
293	    tasks: list[WakeTask] = []
294	    for tid, task in (data.get("tasks") or {}).items():
295	        if not isinstance(task, dict):
296	            continue
297	        label = str(task.get("label") or "")
298	        if not label.startswith(LABEL_PREFIX):
299	            continue
300	        status = _status_name(task.get("status"))
301	        if status == "Done":
302	            continue
303	        pane_id = label[len(LABEL_PREFIX) :]
304	        tasks.append(
305	            WakeTask(
306	                task_id=str(task.get("id", tid)),
307	                pane_id=pane_id,
308	                status=status,
309	                when_display=_datetime_from_status(task),
310	                command=str(task.get("original_command") or task.get("command") or ""),
311	            )
312	        )
313	    return tasks

316	def _rows() -> tuple[list[PaneRec], list[WakeTask]]:
317	    panes = _parse_agent_panes()
318	    tasks = _pueue_tasks()
319	    tasks_by_pane: dict[str, list[WakeTask]] = {}
320	    for task in tasks:
321	        tasks_by_pane.setdefault(task.pane_id, []).append(task)
322	
323	    now = datetime.now().astimezone()
324	    for pane in panes:
325	        text = capture_pane(pane.pane_id or pane.target)
326	        pane.action = recommended_action(text)
327	        msg, reset_epoch, reset_display = detect_quota(active_quota_text(text, pane.action), now)
328	        pane.quota_message = msg
329	        pane.reset_epoch = reset_epoch
330	        pane.reset_display = reset_display
331	        pane_tasks = tasks_by_pane.get(pane.pane_id, [])
332	        if pane_tasks:
333	            pane.state = "SCHEDULED"
334	            pane.scheduled_display = ", ".join(t.when_display or t.status for t in pane_tasks)
335	            pane.scheduled_ids = ",".join(t.task_id for t in pane_tasks)
336	        elif msg and pane.action == ACTION_ENTER:
337	            pane.state = "WAIT_MENU"
338	        elif msg and reset_epoch and reset_epoch <= int(now.timestamp()):
339	            pane.state = "READY"

442	def _delay_arg(args: argparse.Namespace) -> str:

445	        return datetime.fromtimestamp(ts).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
```

```text
199	    lines: list[str] = []
200	    if dump_path and os.path.isfile(dump_path):
201	        with open(dump_path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
202	            lines = [ln.strip() for ln in f if ln.strip()]
203	    else:

205	        histfile = os.environ.get("HISTFILE") or os.path.expanduser("~/.zsh_history")
```

```text
77	_aiagent_autodetect() {
78	  local cand
79	  # Word-split $AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY. The original `${=…}` was zsh's explicit
80	  # word-splitting flag (zsh doesn't split unquoted params by default); bash
81	  # does auto-split unquoted. Dispatch:
82	  local _priority="${AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY:-opencode claude codex cursor-agent}"
83	  if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]; then
84	    setopt local_options sh_word_split

88	    if command -v "$cand" &>/dev/null; then
89	      printf '%s\n' "$cand"
90	      return 0
91	    fi
92	  done
93	  return 1
94	}

96	# Background spinner on stderr while the agent is thinking. Skipped when
97	# AICAP_SPINNER=0 or stderr isn't a tty (so pipes / file redirects stay
98	# clean). The spinner subprocess is disowned via `& disown` so it survives
99	# the command substitution that invokes the agent.
100	_AICAP_SPIN_PID=
101	_aicap_spinner_start() {
102	  [ "$AICAP_SPINNER" != "1" ] && return 0
103	  [ ! -t 2 ] && return 0
104	  local label="${1:-thinking}"
105	  (
106	    trap 'exit 0' TERM INT HUP
107	    local -a frames
108	    frames=('⠋' '⠙' '⠹' '⠸' '⠼' '⠴' '⠦' '⠧' '⠇' '⠏')
109	    local i=0
110	    while true; do
111	      # ${arr[*]:N:1} is bash-style array slicing (0-indexed); zsh supports
112	      # the same syntax. Quoted, a 1-element slice expands as one word.
113	      printf '\r\e[K%s %s' "${frames[*]:$(( i % 10 )):1}" "$label" >&2
114	      i=$(( i + 1 ))
115	      sleep 0.1
116	    done
117	  ) & disown
118	  _AICAP_SPIN_PID=$!
119	}
120	
121	_aicap_spinner_stop() {
122	  [ -z "$_AICAP_SPIN_PID" ] && return 0
123	  kill "$_AICAP_SPIN_PID" 2>/dev/null
124	  # Drain; both shells wait on PIDs even if disowned as long as we know the PID.
125	  wait "$_AICAP_SPIN_PID" 2>/dev/null
126	  _AICAP_SPIN_PID=
127	  [ -t 2 ] && printf '\r\e[K' >&2
128	}

131	# is NOT a tty (so pipes stay clean) or AICAP_PRETTIFY=0.
132	_aicap_prettify() {
133	  if [ "$AICAP_PRETTIFY" != "1" ] || [ ! -t 1 ]; then
134	    cat
135	  elif command -v glow &>/dev/null; then
136	    glow -
137	  elif command -v bat &>/dev/null; then
138	    bat --language=md --style=plain --paging=never --color=always
139	  else

141	  fi

144	# Invoke a coding-agent in one-shot mode.
145	#
146	# Writes reply (text) to stdout. Writes metadata line to stderr when
147	# AICAP_SHOW_METADATA=1 and the agent supports structured JSON output.
148	# Currently only Claude's JSON includes usage/cost — other agents just get a
149	# "<agent> (<model>)" line on stderr.
150	_aiagent_invoke() {
151	  local agent="$1" prompt="$2"
152	  local json reply model_used tokens_in tokens_out cache_read cache_create cost duration rc
153	
154	  # Ensure spinner cleans up if the caller returns or we hit a trap.
155	  trap '_aicap_spinner_stop' EXIT INT TERM
156	
157	  case "$agent" in
158	    claude)
159	      # Conditional --model: empty AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL → claude picks its
160	      # own default (robust if the pinned alias is ever retired).
161	      local -a claude_model_args
162	      claude_model_args=()
163	      [ -n "$AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL" ] && claude_model_args=(--model "$AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL")
164	      local claude_model_label="${AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL:-(default)}"
165	      if [ "$AICAP_SHOW_METADATA" = "1" ] && command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
166	        _aicap_spinner_start "claude $claude_model_label (json)…"
167	        json=$(claude -p "${claude_model_args[@]}" --output-format json "$prompt")
168	        rc=$?
169	        _aicap_spinner_stop
170	        (( rc != 0 )) && return $rc
171	        reply=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.result // empty')
172	        model_used=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.modelUsage | keys | first // "?"')
173	        tokens_in=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.usage.input_tokens // "?"')
174	        tokens_out=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.usage.output_tokens // "?"')
175	        cache_read=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.usage.cache_read_input_tokens // 0')
176	        cache_create=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.usage.cache_creation_input_tokens // 0')
177	        cost=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.total_cost_usd // "?"')
178	        duration=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.duration_ms // "?"')
179	        printf '%s\n' "claude ($model_used) | in=$tokens_in out=$tokens_out cache=(r:$cache_read,w:$cache_create) | cost=\$$cost ${duration}ms" >&2
180	        printf '%s\n' "$reply"
181	      else
182	        printf '%s\n' "claude ($claude_model_label)" >&2
183	        _aicap_spinner_start "claude $claude_model_label…"
184	        claude -p "${claude_model_args[@]}" "$prompt"
185	        rc=$?
186	        _aicap_spinner_stop
187	        return $rc
188	      fi
189	      ;;
190	    opencode)
191	      local -a opencode_model_args
192	      opencode_model_args=()
193	      [ -n "$AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL" ] && opencode_model_args=(-m "$AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL")
194	      local opencode_model_label="${AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL:-(default)}"
195	      printf '%s\n' "opencode ($opencode_model_label)" >&2
196	      _aicap_spinner_start "opencode $opencode_model_label…"
197	      opencode run "${opencode_model_args[@]}" "$prompt"
198	      rc=$?
199	      _aicap_spinner_stop
200	      return $rc
```

```text
67	@dataclass
68	class Config:
69	    name: str             # display name for the markdown table
70	    kind: str             # "cli" or "http"
71	    cmd: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)   # for kind=cli
72	    url: str = ""         # for kind=http

78	def _check_prereqs(c: Config) -> tuple[bool, str]:
79	    if c.kind == "cli":
80	        if not c.cmd:
81	            return False, "empty cmd"
82	        if not shutil.which(c.cmd[0]):
83	            return False, f"{c.cmd[0]!r} not on PATH"
84	        return True, ""
85	    if c.kind == "http":
86	        # Probe URL with a HEAD-ish request; just check connectivity, not auth.
87	        host_probe = c.url.rsplit("/", 3)[0]  # strip /api/v1/chat/completions
88	        try:
89	            req = urllib.request.Request(host_probe, method="GET")
90	            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=2) as _:
91	                pass
92	        except urllib.error.HTTPError:
93	            pass  # 4xx/5xx is fine — server is reachable
94	        except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError):
95	            return False, f"{host_probe} unreachable"
96	        if c.auth_env and not os.environ.get(c.auth_env):
97	            return False, f"{c.auth_env} unset"
98	        return True, ""
99	    return False, f"unknown kind {c.kind!r}"

133	    """Run one invocation; return (ok, wall_seconds, reply_chars, error_snippet)."""

139	            return False, time.perf_counter() - t0, 0, "timeout"
140	        except FileNotFoundError as e:

142	        dt = time.perf_counter() - t0
143	        if r.returncode != 0:
144	            return False, dt, 0, (r.stderr or "rc!=0").strip()[:120]
```

```text
1	# 29_log_tools.sh - Log viewer helpers (tailspin / ccze) (shared bash + zsh).
2	# Moved from dot_config/zsh/tools/29_log_tools.zsh; `emulate -L zsh` gated

4	#
5	# See docs/tools/log-tools.md for the full toolbelt rationale. These thin
6	# wrappers give the "bat for logs" feel without forcing users to remember
7	# each tool's exact flag set.
8	
9	# --- catl: colorful cat for logs (tailspin in stdout mode) ---
10	# Usage: catl app.log | less -R
11	#        catl app.log err.log       (concatenates like cat, colors both)
12	# Requires: tspin (from the tailspin homebrew/GitHub binary, see devtools role).
13	if command -v tspin &>/dev/null; then
14	    catl() {
15	        # `tspin --print` reads from stdin and from positional file args,
16	        # and writes ANSI-colored output to stdout (no pager). That is the
17	        # composition-friendly mode we want for pipes.
18	        command tspin --print "$@"
19	    }
20	fi
21	
22	# --- lessl: classic ccze + less pipeline ---
23	# Usage: lessl app.log
24	#        tail -f app.log | lessl
25	# Requires: ccze, less. Uses -A (raw ANSI) so `less -R` can render colors.
26	if command -v ccze &>/dev/null; then
27	    lessl() {
28	        if (( $# == 0 )); then
29	            command ccze -A | command less -RSFX
30	        else
31	            command ccze -A < "$1" | command less -RSFX
32	        fi
33	    }
34	fi
35	
36	# --- logtail: tail -f with live tailspin highlighting ---
37	# Usage: logtail app.log
38	# Prefers `tspin --follow` (native watch mode) when available; otherwise
39	# falls back to `tail -F | tspin --print` so the highlighting still works on
40	# older tailspin builds that lack --follow.
41	logtail() {
42	    if [[ $# -eq 0 ]]; then
43	        echo "Usage: logtail <file>" >&2
44	        return 2
45	    fi
46	    if command -v tspin &>/dev/null; then
47	        if command tspin --help 2>/dev/null | grep -q -- '--follow'; then
48	            command tspin --follow "$1"
49	        else
50	            command tail -F "$1" | command tspin --print
51	        fi
52	    else
53	        command tail -F "$1"
54	    fi
55	}
56	
57	# --- svclog: follow a service log, cross-platform (systemd / launchd) ---
58	# Usage: svclog SERVICE              (system scope by default)
59	#        svclog --user SERVICE       (systemd user scope on Linux)
60	# On Linux: journalctl -fu SERVICE | tspin
61	# On macOS: tail -F the plist's StdoutPath | tspin, else log stream by process
62	svclog() {
63	    [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ] && emulate -L zsh
64	    local scope=system
65	    if [[ "$1" == "--user" ]]; then
66	        scope=user
67	        shift
68	    fi
69	    if [[ $# -eq 0 ]]; then
70	        echo "Usage: svclog [--user] <service>" >&2
71	        return 2
72	    fi
73	    local name="$1"
74	    local os
75	    os="$(uname -s)"
76	    local colorize='if command -v tspin &>/dev/null; then tspin --print; else cat; fi'
77	
78	    if [[ "$os" == "Linux" ]]; then
79	        if [[ "$scope" == user ]]; then
80	            journalctl --user -fu "$name" | eval "$colorize"
81	        else
82	            if sudo -n true 2>/dev/null; then
83	                sudo journalctl -fu "$name" | eval "$colorize"
84	            else
85	                journalctl -fu "$name" | eval "$colorize"
86	            fi
87	        fi
88	    elif [[ "$os" == "Darwin" ]]; then
89	        local dom
90	        if [[ "$scope" == user ]]; then
91	            dom="gui/${UID:-$(id -u)}"
92	        else
93	            dom="system"
94	        fi
95	        local path
96	        path="$(launchctl print "$dom/$name" 2>/dev/null \
97	            | awk -F'= ' '/^[ \t]+stdout path / || /^[ \t]+standard out path /{gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/,"",$2); print $2; exit}')"
98	        if [[ -n "$path" && -f "$path" ]]; then
99	            tail -F "$path" | eval "$colorize"
100	        else
101	            echo "[svclog] No StdoutPath for $dom/$name — streaming via log stream..."
102	            log stream --predicate "process == \"$name\"" --style syslog | eval "$colorize"
103	        fi
104	    else
105	        echo "svclog: unsupported OS: $os" >&2
106	        return 1
107	    fi
108	}
109

111	# Usage: svcstat SERVICE           (system scope on both OSes)
112	#        svcstat --user SERVICE    (systemd user scope / macOS gui domain)
113	svcstat() {
114	    [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ] && emulate -L zsh
115	    local scope=system
116	    if [[ "$1" == "--user" ]]; then
117	        scope=user
118	        shift
119	    fi
120	    if [[ $# -eq 0 ]]; then
121	        echo "Usage: svcstat [--user] <service>" >&2
122	        return 2
123	    fi
124	    local name="$1"
125	    local os
126	    os="$(uname -s)"
127	    if [[ "$os" == "Linux" ]]; then
128	        if [[ "$scope" == user ]]; then
129	            systemctl --user status "$name" --no-pager -l
130	        else
131	            systemctl status "$name" --no-pager -l
132	        fi
133	    elif [[ "$os" == "Darwin" ]]; then
134	        local dom
135	        if [[ "$scope" == user ]]; then
136	            dom="gui/${UID:-$(id -u)}"
137	        else
138	            dom="system"
139	        fi
140	        launchctl print "$dom/$name" 2>/dev/null \
141	            || { [[ "$scope" == system ]] && sudo launchctl print "system/$name"; } \
142	            || echo "No launchctl print output for $dom/$name"
143	    else
144	        echo "svcstat: unsupported OS: $os" >&2
145	        return 1
146	    fi
147	}
```

34	
35	## Goal
36	
37	Replace the "staring at `systemctl list-units` through less" experience with a pueue-style `tv services` picker that works on both Linux (systemd) and macOS (launchd), with tailspin-colored log preview and Alt-key lifecycle actions. Implement the unified channel first; deeper per-OS channels are scoped as follow-up phases.
38	
39	## Model cheat sheet (why we need a template, not raw if-else)
40	
41	```mermaid
42	flowchart LR
43	  subgraph linux [Linux / systemd]
44	    sc[systemctl]
45	    jc[journalctl -u UNIT]
46	    sc --> sc_list["list-units --state=running|failed|all"]
47	    sc --> sc_files["list-unit-files (on-disk, w/ enabled|disabled|static|masked)"]
48	    sc --> sc_ctl["start | stop | restart | reload | enable | disable"]
49	    sc --> sc_user["--user (per-user scope)"]
50	    etc["/etc/systemd/system/<br/>~/.config/systemd/user/<br/>(admin inventory)"] -.discoverable via fd.-> sc_files
51	  end
52	  subgraph darwin [macOS / launchd]
53	    lc[launchctl]
54	    lc --> lc_list["list (PID  Status  Label)"]
55	    lc --> lc_print["print system/LABEL or gui/UID/LABEL"]
56	    lc --> lc_disabled["print-disabled system/ + gui/UID"]
57	    lc --> lc_ctl["kickstart -k | bootout | bootstrap | enable | disable"]
58	    libLaunch["/Library/LaunchDaemons/<br/>/Library/LaunchAgents/<br/>~/Library/LaunchAgents/<br/>(plists on disk)"] -.discoverable via fd.-> lc_list
59	    logShow["log show --predicate 'process == LABEL'"]
60	    stdoutTail["tail -F StdoutPath (from launchctl print)"]
61	  end
62	```
63	
64	Same concept, very different commands. The unified channel paper-overs them with a chezmoi template; power-user channels live as OS-specific templates.
65	
66	## Phase 1 (this change): unified `tv services` channel
67	
68	### 1. New file: [`dot_config/television/cable/services.toml.tmpl`](dot_config/television/cable/services.toml.tmpl)
69	
70	Modeled on [`dot_config/television/cable/pueue.toml`](dot_config/television/cable/pueue.toml) — same tab-separated row format, same Alt-key muscle memory, same `watch = 2.0` refresh.
71	
72	Row format (uniform across OSes): `SYMBOL\tNAME\tSCOPE\tINFO`
73	
74	- `SYMBOL`: `▶ Running` / `✗ Failed` / `⏸ Stopped` / `? Unknown` for runtime cycles (1–4). For cycle 5 (on-disk view), the symbol instead carries enablement state so "configured but not enabled" pops out visually:
75	  - Linux: `✓ Enabled` / `○ Disabled` / `— Static` / `⊘ Masked` / `↪ Alias` / `● Indirect`
76	  - macOS: `● Loaded` (running or scheduled) / `○ On-disk` (plist present, not loaded) / `⊘ Disabled` (in `launchctl print-disabled`)
77	- `NAME`: unit name (Linux: `nginx.service`) or label (macOS: `com.apple.nsurlsessiond`)
78	- `SCOPE`: `system` or `user`
79	- `INFO`: description (Linux, cycles 1–4) / enablement or PID (cycle 5) / `PID=…` / `exit=N` (macOS)
80	
81	Display string: `"{split:\\t:0}  {split:\\t:1}  [{split:\\t:2}]  {split:\\t:3}"`
82	Output (for actions): `"{split:\\t:1}|{split:\\t:2}"` — name + scope so actions know whether to sudo.
83	
84	#### 5 source cycles (Ctrl+S)
85	
86	1. **Running only** — currently active services, system+user merged
87	2. **All loaded** — active + inactive + failed among *loaded* units (includes runtime-only and transient units)
88	3. **Failed only** — crashed / non-zero exit
89	4. **User-scope only** — `systemctl --user` / macOS `gui/$UID/` domain
90	5. **Installed (on-disk)** — every unit file systemd knows about (Linux) or every `.plist` under the launchd search paths (macOS). This is the "configured but not enabled" discovery view, and is a strict superset of cycle 2 for services that have unit files. Landing on a `○ Disabled` row and hitting `Alt+L` toggles it on at boot.
91	
92	> Why cycle 5 differs from cycle 2 (Linux specifically): `list-units` only shows units systemd currently has loaded (active, inactive, failed). `list-unit-files` shows every unit file on disk including ones that have never been instantiated — that's where "I dropped this .service into /etc/systemd/system/ but forgot to enable it" hides.
93	
94	Per-OS commands (templated with `{{ if eq .chezmoi.os "linux" }}` / `{{ else }}` / `{{ end }}`):
95	
96	- **Linux**:
97	  - Running: `systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running --no-legend --plain --no-pager` then awk → row format; append `--user` variant tagged `user`.
98	  - All loaded: same with `--all` (no `--state`).
99	  - Failed: `--state=failed`.
100	  - User-scope: `systemctl --user list-units --type=service --all ...`.
101	  - Installed: `systemctl list-unit-files --type=service --no-legend --no-pager --plain` (system scope) merged with `systemctl --user list-unit-files --type=service --no-legend --no-pager --plain` (user scope). Awk maps the STATE column (`enabled|disabled|static|masked|alias|indirect|generated|transient`) to the symbols above. The unit-file path is derivable on-demand for the `Alt+E` edit action via `systemctl [--user] cat NAME | head -1`.
102	- **macOS**:
103	  - Running: `launchctl list | awk 'NR>1 && $1 != "-" ...'` → user scope; `sudo -n launchctl list` output merged for system scope when passwordless sudo succeeds; otherwise user scope only, with an informational row explaining sudo is needed to see system daemons.
104	  - All loaded: `launchctl list` (all rows) + sudo variant.
105	  - Failed: `awk '$2 != 0 && $2 != "Status"'`.
106	  - User-scope: `launchctl list` without sudo.
107	  - Column enrichment: `launchctl list` has no description, so INFO column carries `PID=N` or `exit=N`.
108	  - Installed (on-disk): `fd -HI '.plist$' /Library/LaunchDaemons /Library/LaunchAgents "$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents" 2>/dev/null` for admin- and user-installed jobs. Apple's `/System/Library/Launch*` is excluded by default (~600 noisy rows) but documented as a one-line opt-in edit. Awk derives label from the plist filename (`basename .plist`), scope from path (`/Library/LaunchDaemons` → system-daemon, `/Library/LaunchAgents` → system-agent, `~/Library/LaunchAgents` → user), and correlates with a one-shot `launchctl list | awk 'NR>1{print $3}'` lookup to mark `● Loaded` vs `○ On-disk`; `launchctl print-disabled system/` and `launchctl print-disabled gui/$UID` fill in `⊘ Disabled`.
109	
110	#### 2 preview cycles (Ctrl+F)
111	
112	1. **Colorful log tail via tailspin** — last ~500 lines through `tspin --print`:
113	   - Linux: `journalctl --no-pager --user? -u NAME -n 500` (picks `--user` flag if scope=user, else system).
114	   - macOS: try `tail -n 500 $(launchctl print DOMAIN/LABEL | awk -F'= ' '/stdout path/{print $2; exit}')`; if the plist has no StdoutPath, fall back to `log show --predicate 'process == "LABEL"' --last 1h --style syslog`.
115	2. **Status / details**:
116	   - Linux: `systemctl [--user] status NAME --no-pager -l -n 0` (just the status block, log preview is in cycle 1).
117	   - macOS: `launchctl print DOMAIN/LABEL` (full block: state, paths, spawn policy, last exit).
118	
119	#### Keybindings (Alt-keys, match pueue semantics)
120	
121	- `Enter` → follow live: Linux `journalctl -fu NAME`, macOS `tail -F StdoutPath | tspin --print` (or `log stream --predicate ...` fallback). Wraps with `echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _` for graceful exit.
122	- `Alt+R` → restart: `systemctl [--user] restart NAME` / `launchctl kickstart -k DOMAIN/LABEL`. Auto-prepends `sudo` when scope=system.
123	- `Alt+S` → stop: `systemctl stop` / `launchctl bootout DOMAIN/LABEL`.
124	- `Alt+T` → start: `systemctl start` / `launchctl bootstrap DOMAIN PATH_TO_PLIST`. (Start on macOS is tricky without knowing the plist path — fallback to `kickstart` for already-loaded jobs.)
125	- `Alt+U` → reload: `systemctl reload-or-restart` / `launchctl kickstart` (no `-k`).
126	- `Alt+D` → status details: switches preview to cycle 2 equivalent in a full pager (execute mode).
127	- `Alt+E` → edit: Linux `sudo systemctl edit --full NAME`; macOS opens the plist in `$EDITOR` by reading path from `launchctl print`.
128	- `Alt+L` → toggle enable on boot: `systemctl [--user] enable/disable NAME` (parse current state first) / `launchctl enable/disable DOMAIN/LABEL`.
129	- `Ctrl+Y` → copy name: OSC 52 clipboard helper (copy-pattern from pueue's `copy_command`).
130	
131	All mutating actions `reload_source` like pueue's lifecycle actions.
132	
133	#### Sudo strategy
134	
135	Scope tag in the output (`name|scope`) tells the action whether to prepend `sudo`. Actions use `execute` mode (not `fork`) so sudo can prompt in the subshell terminal. If `sudo -n true` succeeds the prompt is invisible; otherwise the user sees the standard password prompt then Enter to return to tv.

**Key patterns:**
- `pueue group add <GROUP_NAME>` — create group (idempotent; safe to call repeatedly)
- `pueue parallel -g <GROUP> 1` — set parallelism to 1 (sequential execution)
- `pueue add -g <GROUP> --label "<LABEL>" --delay <DELAY> "<COMMAND>"` — queue task

  - `<DELAY>` can be relative (`"70m"`) or absolute time expression
  - `--print-task-id` outputs the task ID to stdout for tracking

```bash
# Initialize (call once)

pueue parallel -g agent-warmup 1

# Add a delayed task
pueue add -g agent-warmup \
  --label "agent-warmup:$(date +%s)" \
  --delay "2h" \
  --print-task-id \
  "claude -p 'continue'"
```

```md
# Plan: `agent-warmup` — interactive Claude quota-window warmup

## Context

**Goal.** Automatically start the Claude Pro/Max **5-hour subscription usage
window** at a fixed time (e.g. 06:00 on workdays), so a fresh window is already
running before the user begins real work — plus an ad-hoc "warm up at this time"
one-shot. This implements [backlog/agent-quota-warmup-at-time.md](../../backlog/agent-quota-warmup-at-time.md).

**Why the obvious design is wrong (key finding).** The backlog's candidate v1
("isolated cwd + `claude -p 'Reply exactly: hi'`") is **obsolete as of the
June 15, 2026 Anthropic billing split.** Web research (corroborated across
multiple sources) confirms:

- The 5-hour window is triggered **only by interactive usage** — interactive
  Claude.ai chat and **interactive terminal Claude Code** advance/start it.
- **Headless `claude -p`** (plus Agent SDK, GitHub Actions, third-party agents)
  now draws from a **separate metered Agent SDK credit pool** (~$20 Pro /
  $100 Max5x / $200 Max20x, API rates, no rollover). Framing: *"if a human
  presses enter you stay on subscription; if a robot presses enter while you're
  away, that usage moves to the metered credit."*

So a `claude -p` warmup would **silently burn API credit and never move the
window**. The only mechanism that can move the 5-hour window is a **genuine
interactive Claude Code TUI session**. The realistic automated form of that:
launch real interactive `claude` in a **detached tmux session** (PTY-backed,
subscription auth, isolated cwd), then `tmux send-keys` a tiny prompt + Enter.

**Residual uncertainty (must verify empirically).** Whether Anthropic still
classifies a *tmux-driven* interactive session as "interactive" is unconfirmed.
The billing system almost certainly keys off client/session **type**, not who
physically pressed Enter, so a real interactive TUI should count — but the plan
includes a manual verification step before trusting the recurring install.

**Decisions captured from the user:**
- Pivot to **interactive-tmux** warmup (only thing that can move the window).
- Support **recurring** (launchd/systemd timer) **+ one-shot** (pueue).
- **Standalone** tool — leave `agent-wakeup`, the delayed-run scheduler, and the
  dashboard-TUI as separate backlog items.
- Also apply **code-quality fixes** to the existing Codex `agent-wakeup` (no
  history rewrite), with conventional commit messages.

## Design overview

New single-file uv-script CLI **`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_agent-warmup`**
(PEP 723, `argparse`), mirroring the `executable_pqsum` pattern (on `~/.dotfiles/bin`
PATH, no shell wrapper needed). Claude-only (per backlog; Codex/OpenCode have
different quota systems).

Core mechanism reuses the proven interactive-spawn pattern from
`dot_config/shell/22_sesh.sh` (`tmux new-session -d ... "claude"`) and the pueue
group convention from `dot_config/television/executable_agent-wakeup.py:458`.

**Isolation choices:**
- Dedicated tmux socket `tmux -L agent-warmup` — keeps warmup sessions out of the
  user's main server/workspace and independent of it.
- Isolated cwd `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/agent-warmup/claude` — no project
  `CLAUDE.md`/context. (Cache convention per `executable_lan-scan.sh`.)
- Bare `claude` (NOT `specstory run claude`) so no transcript is saved; NOT
  `--bare` (that forces `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` = API billing, defeating the purpose).
  Default `--model haiku` (matches `AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL` default in
  `dot_config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh:44`) to keep window-token consumption tiny.
- Force subscription auth: `unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the spawned env.

### Subcommands

| Command | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `agent-warmup run [--model H] [--prompt P] [--timeout S] [--keep] [--verify]` | Spawn detached tmux + interactive `claude` in isolated cwd; wait for ready; handle first-run folder-trust prompt; send prompt + Enter; wait for a reply; optionally send `/usage` and capture the panel (`--verify`); log to `run-<ts>.log`; kill session unless `--keep`; notify on failure. |
| `agent-warmup at (--at EXPR \| --delay EXPR) [run-flags]` | Queue a one-shot `agent-warmup run` via pueue (`--delay`/absolute), group `agent-warmup`, label `agent-warmup:oneshot:<ts>`. |
| `agent-warmup install (--daily DAYS --time HH:MM) [run-flags]` | Generate + load a recurring timer: macOS LaunchAgent (`StartCalendarInterval`) or Linux systemd user `.service`+`.timer`. Imperative/opt-in, written outside chezmoi management. |
| `agent-warmup uninstall` | Unload + remove the generated timer. |
| `agent-warmup status [--json]` | Show pending pueue one-shots + installed timer state + last N `run-*.log` summaries (timestamp, exit, whether `/usage` captured). |
| `agent-warmup cancel` | Remove pending pueue one-shots for this tool. |
| `agent-warmup verify` | Alias for `run --verify --keep` — the empirical experiment helper; prints the `/usage` panel for the user to eyeball. |

### `run` orchestration detail
1. `mkdir -p` cache + isolated cwd; acquire a lockfile (refuse if a prior warmup
   session is still alive — clean up stale ones).
2. `tmux -L agent-warmup new-session -d -s warmup-<ts> -c <isolated-cwd>` with env
   `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` unset, running `claude --model <model>`.
3. Poll `tmux -L agent-warmup capture-pane` until the input box is ready; if a
   folder-trust prompt appears ("Do you trust the files…"), send Enter to accept
   (or pre-seed trust in the isolated `.claude/`). **Gotcha to handle.**
4. `send-keys` the prompt text, then `Enter` (mirror agent-wakeup's `C-u TEXT Enter`).
5. Poll until a response renders or `--timeout` (default ~90s) elapses.
6. If `--verify`: `send-keys "/usage" Enter`, wait, capture the rendered panel.
7. Capture final pane → append to `run-<ts>.log` with ISO timestamp + exit status.
8. `kill-session` unless `--keep`. On any failure (timeout, claude exited
   non-zero, auth error), emit a desktop notification.

### Notifications (no shared helper exists — add a tiny internal one)
The repo has no central notify utility. Add a small internal function:
`osascript -e 'display notification …'` on darwin, `notify-send` on Linux (guarded
by `command -v`), always also print to stderr. Keep it inside the script.

### Recurring timer generation
- **macOS** → `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.<user>.agent-warmup.plist` with
  `StartCalendarInterval` (array of `{Weekday, Hour, Minute}` for the requested
  days/time), `ProgramArguments = [<abs path to>/agent-warmup, run]`, explicit
  `PATH` in `EnvironmentVariables` (chezmoi→cargo→uv→~/bin→brew, mirroring
  `scripts/fleet/exec.py:_PATH_PRELUDE`) since launchd has a minimal env. Load via
  `launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) <plist>`. Validate with **`plutil -lint`**.
- **Linux** → `~/.config/systemd/user/agent-warmup.{service,timer}`; `service`
  is `Type=oneshot` calling `agent-warmup run`; `timer` uses `OnCalendar=`.
  `systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user enable --now agent-warmup.timer`.
  Validate with **`systemd-analyze verify`**.
- Caveat to document: if the machine is asleep at the scheduled time, the job
  fires on wake (launchd coalesces; systemd `Persistent=true`) — so window
  geometry may shift. Keychain must be unlocked (user logged in) for subscription
  auth to work from launchd.

## Critical files

- **New:** `dot_config/zsh/tools/49_agent_warmup_completion.zsh` +

## Cross-file maintenance (per CLAUDE.md)
```

The plan is written. Here's the summary of what I'm proposing:

## TL;DR

The headline finding from research changed the design: **the June 15, 2026 Anthropic billing split means headless `claude -p` no longer moves the 5-hour subscription window** — it draws from a separate metered Agent SDK credit pool. The backlog's original "isolated cwd + `claude -p`" design would silently burn API credit and accomplish nothing. **Only genuine interactive Claude Code usage moves the window.**

So the plan pivots to a new standalone CLI **`agent-warmup`** (single-file uv-script in `dot_dotfiles/bin/`, like `pqsum`) that:

- **`run`** — spawns a *real interactive* `claude` TUI in a **detached tmux session** (dedicated socket, isolated cache cwd, subscription auth, `--model haiku`), sends a tiny prompt + Enter, logs the result, and can capture `/usage` for audit.
- **`at`** — pueue one-shot ("warm up tomorrow 06:00").
- **`install`/`uninstall`** — recurring macOS launchd / Linux systemd user timer, generated imperatively (opt-in, no chezmoi-prompt churn).

```text
## Approved Plan:
# Plan: `agent-warmup` — interactive Claude quota-window warmup

## Context

**Goal.** Automatically start the Claude Pro/Max **5-hour subscription usage
window** at a fixed time (e.g. 06:00 on workdays), so a fresh window is already
running before the user begins real work — plus an ad-hoc "warm up at this time"
one-shot. This implements [backlog/agent-quota-warmup-at-time.md](../../backlog/agent-quota-warmup-at-time.md).

**Why the obvious design is wrong (key finding).** The backlog's candidate v1
("isolated cwd + `claude -p 'Reply exactly: hi'`") is **obsolete as of the
June 15, 2026 Anthropic billing split.** Web research (corroborated across
multiple sources) confirms:

- The 5-hour window is triggered **only by interactive usage** — interactive
  Claude.ai chat and **interactive terminal Claude Code** advance/start it.
- **Headless `claude -p`** (plus Agent SDK, GitHub Actions, third-party agents)
  now draws from a **separate metered Agent SDK credit pool** (~$20 Pro /
  $100 Max5x / $200 Max20x, API rates, no rollover). Framing: *"if a human
  presses enter you stay on subscription; if a robot presses enter while you're
  away, that usage moves to the metered credit."*

So a `claude -p` warmup would **silently burn API credit and never move the
window**. The only mechanism that can move the 5-hour window is a **genuine
interactive Claude Code TUI session**. The realistic automated form of that:
launch real interactive `claude` in a **detached tmux session** (PTY-backed,
subscription auth, isolated cwd), then `tmux send-keys` a tiny prompt + Enter.

**Residual uncertainty (must verify empirically).** Whether Anthropic still
classifies a *tmux-driven* interactive session as "interactive" is unconfirmed.
The billing system almost certainly keys off client/session **type**, not who
physically pressed Enter, so a real interactive TUI should count — but the plan
includes a manual verification step before trusting the recurring install.

**Decisions captured from the user:**
- Pivot to **interactive-tmux** warmup (only thing that can move the window).
- Support **recurring** (launchd/systemd timer) **+ one-shot** (pueue).
- **Standalone** tool — leave `agent-wakeup`, the delayed-run scheduler, and the
  dashboard-TUI as separate backlog items.
- Also apply **code-quality fixes** to the existing Codex `agent-wakeup` (no
  history rewrite), with conventional commit messages.

## Design overview

New single-file uv-script CLI **`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_agent-warmup`**
(PEP 723, `argparse`), mirroring the `executable_pqsum` pattern (on `~/.dotfiles/bin`
PATH, no shell wrapper needed). Claude-only (per backlog; Codex/OpenCode have
different quota systems).

Core mechanism reuses the proven interactive-spawn pattern from
`dot_config/shell/22_sesh.sh` (`tmux new-session -d ... "claude"`) and the pueue
group convention from `dot_config/television/executable_agent-wakeup.py:458`.

**Isolation choices:**
- Dedicated tmux socket `tmux -L agent-warmup` — keeps warmup sessions out of the
  user's main server/workspace and independent of it.
- Isolated cwd `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/agent-warmup/claude` — no project
  `CLAUDE.md`/context. (Cache convention per `executable_lan-scan.sh`.)
- Bare `claude` (NOT `specstory run claude`) so no transcript is saved; NOT
  `--bare` (that forces `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` = API billing, defeating the purpose).
  Default `--model haiku` (matches `AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL` default in
  `dot_config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh:44`) to keep window-token consumption tiny.
- Force subscription auth: `unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the spawned env.

### Subcommands

| Command | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `agent-warmup run [--model H] [--prompt P] [--timeout S] [--keep] [--verify]` | Spawn detached tmux + interactive `claude` in isolated cwd; wait for ready; handle first-run folder-trust prompt; send prompt + Enter; wait for a reply; optionally send `/usage` and capture the panel (`--verify`); log to `run-<ts>.log`; kill session unless `--keep`; notify on failure. |
| `agent-warmup at (--at EXPR \| --delay EXPR) [run-flags]` | Queue a one-shot `agent-warmup run` via pueue (`--delay`/absolute), group `agent-warmup`, label `agent-warmup:oneshot:<ts>`. |
| `agent-warmup install (--daily DAYS --time HH:MM) [run-flags]` | Generate + load a recurring timer: macOS LaunchAgent (`StartCalendarInterval`) or Linux systemd user `.service`+`.timer`. Imperative/opt-in, written outside chezmoi management. |
| `agent-warmup uninstall` | Unload + remove the generated timer. |
| `agent-warmup status [--json]` | Show pending pueue one-shots + installed timer state + last N `run-*.log` summaries (timestamp, exit, whether `/usage` captured). |
| `agent-warmup cancel` | Remove pending pueue one-shots for this tool. |
| `agent-warmup verify` | Alias for `run --verify --keep` — the empirical experiment helper; prints the `/usage` panel for the user to eyeball. |

### `run` orchestration detail
1. `mkdir -p` cache + isolated cwd; acquire a lockfile (refuse if a prior warmup
   session is still alive — clean up stale ones).
2. `tmux -L agent-warmup new-session -d -s warmup-<ts> -c <isolated-cwd>` with env
   `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` unset, running `claude --model <model>`.
3. Poll `tmux -L agent-warmup capture-pane` until the input box is ready; if a
   folder-trust prompt appears ("Do you trust the files…"), send Enter to accept
   (or pre-seed trust in the isolated `.claude/`). **Gotcha to handle.**
4. `send-keys` the prompt text, then `Enter` (mirror agent-wakeup's `C-u TEXT Enter`).
5. Poll until a response renders or `--timeout` (default ~90s) elapses.
6. If `--verify`: `send-keys "/usage" Enter`, wait, capture the rendered panel.
7. Capture final pane → append to `run-<ts>.log` with ISO timestamp + exit status.
8. `kill-session` unless `--keep`. On any failure (timeout, claude exited
   non-zero, auth error), emit a desktop notification.

### Notifications (no shared helper exists — add a tiny internal one)
The repo has no central notify utility. Add a small internal function:
`osascript -e 'display notification …'` on darwin, `notify-send` on Linux (guarded
by `command -v`), always also print to stderr. Keep it inside the script.

### Recurring timer generation
- **macOS** → `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.<user>.agent-warmup.plist` with
  `StartCalendarInterval` (array of `{Weekday, Hour, Minute}` for the requested
  days/time), `ProgramArguments = [<abs path to>/agent-warmup, run]`, explicit
  `PATH` in `EnvironmentVariables` (chezmoi→cargo→uv→~/bin→brew, mirroring
  `scripts/fleet/exec.py:_PATH_PRELUDE`) since launchd has a minimal env. Load via
  `launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) <plist>`. Validate with **`plutil -lint`**.
- **Linux** → `~/.config/systemd/user/agent-warmup.{service,timer}`; `service`
  is `Type=oneshot` calling `agent-warmup run`; `timer` uses `OnCalendar=`.
  `systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user enable --now agent-warmup.timer`.
  Validate with **`systemd-analyze verify`**.
- Caveat to document: if the machine is asleep at the scheduled time, the job
  fires on wake (launchd coalesces; systemd `Persistent=true`) — so window
  geometry may shift. Keychain must be unlocked (user logged in) for subscription
  auth to work from launchd.
```

```text
157	def _is_claude_hud_usage_line(line: str) -> bool:
158	    """claude-hud statusLine usage is cached/non-authoritative for wakeups."""
159	    plain = _strip_ansi(line).strip()

169	def _parse_reset_expr(expr: str, now: datetime) -> datetime | None:
170	    expr = expr.strip()
171	    expr = re.split(r"\s*[·|]\s*", expr, maxsplit=1)[0].strip()
172	    expr = re.sub(r"\s*\([^)]*\)\s*$", "", expr).strip()
173	    expr = expr.rstrip(".,; ")
174	
175	    m = re.search(
176	        r"(?:(\d+)\s*h(?:ours?)?)?\s*(?:(\d+)\s*m(?:in(?:ute)?s?)?)",
177	        expr,
178	        re.IGNORECASE,
179	    )
180	    if m and (m.group(1) or m.group(2)):
181	        hours = int(m.group(1) or 0)
182	        mins = int(m.group(2) or 0)
183	        return now + timedelta(hours=hours, minutes=mins)
184	
185	    m = re.search(r"\b(\d+)\s*(?:seconds?|secs?|s)\b", expr, re.IGNORECASE)
186	    if m:
187	        return now + timedelta(seconds=int(m.group(1)))
188	
189	    m = re.search(r"\b(\d+)\s*(?:days?|d)\b", expr, re.IGNORECASE)
190	    if m:
191	        return now + timedelta(days=int(m.group(1)))
192	
193	    time_match = re.search(r"\b(\d{1,2})(?::(\d{2}))?\s*(am|pm)?\b", expr, re.IGNORECASE)
194	    if time_match:
195	        hour = int(time_match.group(1))
196	        minute = int(time_match.group(2) or 0)
197	        ampm = (time_match.group(3) or "").lower()
198	        if ampm == "pm" and hour < 12:
199	            hour += 12
200	        elif ampm == "am" and hour == 12:
201	            hour = 0
202	        if hour > 23 or minute > 59:
203	            return None
204	        dt = now.replace(hour=hour, minute=minute, second=0, microsecond=0)
205	        if dt <= now:
206	            dt += timedelta(days=1)
207	        return dt
208	
209	    return None

212	def detect_quota(text: str, now: datetime | None = None) -> tuple[str, int, str]:
213	    now = now or datetime.now().astimezone()
214	    quota_lines = [
215	        line.strip()
216	        for line in text.splitlines()
217	        if _QUOTA_LINE_RE.search(line) and not _is_claude_hud_usage_line(line)
218	    ]
219	    if not quota_lines:
220	        return ("", 0, "")
221	
222	    reset_dt: datetime | None = None
223	    chosen = quota_lines[-1]
224	    for line in reversed(quota_lines):
225	        m = _RESET_RE.search(line)

244	def active_quota_text(text: str, action: str) -> str:

250	def _status_name(status: Any) -> str:
251	    if isinstance(status, str):
252	        return status
253	    if isinstance(status, dict) and status:
254	        return next(iter(status.keys()))
255	    return str(status)

258	def _datetime_from_status(task: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
259	    candidates: list[str] = []
260	
261	    def walk(v: Any) -> None:
262	        if isinstance(v, dict):
263	            for key, val in v.items():
264	                if key in {"enqueue_at", "enqueued_at", "start", "created_at"} and isinstance(val, str):
265	                    candidates.append(val)
266	                walk(val)
267	        elif isinstance(v, list):
268	            for item in v:
269	                walk(item)
270	
271	    walk(task.get("status"))
272	    if isinstance(task.get("created_at"), str):
273	        candidates.append(str(task["created_at"]))
274	    for value in candidates:
275	        try:
276	            return _format_dt(datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace("Z", "+00:00")).astimezone())
277	        except ValueError:
278	            continue
279	    return ""

282	def _pueue_tasks() -> list[WakeTask]:
283	    if not shutil.which("pueue"):
284	        return []
285	    cp = run(["pueue", "status", "--json"])
286	    if cp.returncode != 0:
287	        return []
288	    try:
289	        data = json.loads(cp.stdout)
290	    except json.JSONDecodeError:
291	        return []
292	
293	    tasks: list[WakeTask] = []
294	    for tid, task in (data.get("tasks") or {}).items():
295	        if not isinstance(task, dict):
296	            continue
297	        label = str(task.get("label") or "")
298	        if not label.startswith(LABEL_PREFIX):
299	            continue
300	        status = _status_name(task.get("status"))
301	        if status == "Done":
302	            continue
303	        pane_id = label[len(LABEL_PREFIX) :]
304	        tasks.append(
305	            WakeTask(
306	                task_id=str(task.get("id", tid)),
307	                pane_id=pane_id,
308	                status=status,
309	                when_display=_datetime_from_status(task),
310	                command=str(task.get("original_command") or task.get("command") or ""),
311	            )
312	        )
313	    return tasks

316	def _rows() -> tuple[list[PaneRec], list[WakeTask]]:
317	    panes = _parse_agent_panes()
318	    tasks = _pueue_tasks()
319	    tasks_by_pane: dict[str, list[WakeTask]] = {}
320	    for task in tasks:
321	        tasks_by_pane.setdefault(task.pane_id, []).append(task)
322	
323	    now = datetime.now().astimezone()
324	    for pane in panes:
325	        text = capture_pane(pane.pane_id or pane.target)
326	        pane.action = recommended_action(text)
327	        msg, reset_epoch, reset_display = detect_quota(active_quota_text(text, pane.action), now)
328	        pane.quota_message = msg
329	        pane.reset_epoch = reset_epoch
330	        pane.reset_display = reset_display
331	        pane_tasks = tasks_by_pane.get(pane.pane_id, [])
332	        if pane_tasks:
333	            pane.state = "SCHEDULED"
334	            pane.scheduled_display = ", ".join(t.when_display or t.status for t in pane_tasks)
335	            pane.scheduled_ids = ",".join(t.task_id for t in pane_tasks)
336	        elif msg and pane.action == ACTION_ENTER:
337	            pane.state = "WAIT_MENU"
338	        elif msg and reset_epoch and reset_epoch <= int(now.timestamp()):
339	            pane.state = "READY"
340	        elif msg:
341	            pane.state = "WAIT_QUOTA"
342	        elif pane.glyph == "●":
343	            pane.state = "ACTIVE"
344	        elif pane.glyph == "○":
345	            pane.state = "IDLE"
346	        else:
347	            pane.state = "UNKNOWN"
348	
349	    live_ids = {p.pane_id for p in panes if p.pane_id}
350	    for task in tasks:
351	        if task.pane_id in live_ids:
352	            continue
353	        panes.append(
354	            PaneRec(
355	                agent="[??]",
356	                when="",
357	                sid="",
358	                cwd="?",
359	                title="queued wakeup for missing pane",
360	                specstory="",
361	                target=task.pane_id,
362	                pane_pid="",
363	                glyph="",
364	                pane_id=task.pane_id,
365	                state="ORPHAN",
366	                scheduled_display=task.when_display or task.status,
367	                scheduled_ids=task.task_id,
368	            )
369	        )
370	
371	    return panes, tasks

613	def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
614	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="agent-wakeup")
615	    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=False)
616	
617	    s = sub.add_parser("status", help="Show live agent panes and wakeup tasks")
618	    s.add_argument("--tsv", action="store_true", help="Print TV-friendly TSV")
619	    s.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="Print JSON")
620	    s.set_defaults(func=cmd_status)

622	    s = sub.add_parser("schedule", help="Schedule a continue for a pane")
623	    s.add_argument("--pane", help="tmux pane target or pane id")
624	    s.add_argument("--current", action="store_true", help="Use $TMUX_PANE")
625	    s.add_argument("--at", help="Absolute time expression for pueue --delay")
626	    s.add_argument("--delay", help="Relative delay for pueue --delay, e.g. 70m")
627	    s.add_argument("--when", help="Time/delay expression; relative forms use pueue --delay")
628	    s.add_argument("--at-epoch", type=int, help="Epoch seconds, converted to local time")
629	    s.add_argument("--buffer-minutes", type=int, default=0, help="Add minutes to --at-epoch")
630	    s.add_argument("--text", default=DEFAULT_TEXT, help="Text to send before Enter")

638	    s = sub.add_parser("send-now", help="Send continue to a pane now")
639	    s.add_argument("--pane", help="tmux pane target or pane id")
640	    s.add_argument("--current", action="store_true", help="Use $TMUX_PANE")
641	    s.add_argument("--text", default=DEFAULT_TEXT)
642	    s.add_argument("--enter-only", action="store_true", help="Send only Enter")
643	    s.add_argument("--auto", action="store_true", help="Choose Enter for rate-limit menus, otherwise continue")

659	    return p
```

```
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = []
# ///
"""agent-warmup — start the Claude Pro/Max 5-hour subscription window on a schedule.

Why interactive (and not ``claude -p``):
  Since the 2026-06-15 Anthropic billing split, only *interactive* Claude Code
  usage advances the rolling 5-hour subscription window. Headless ``claude -p``
  (and the Agent SDK) draw from a separate metered credit pool and do NOT move
  the window. So to "warm up" the window we must drive a real interactive
  ``claude`` TUI: this tool launches one in a detached tmux session (dedicated
  socket, isolated cwd, subscription auth), sends a tiny prompt + Enter, then
  tears the session down. See pitfalls/headless-claude-p-does-not-move-5h-window.md.

  Whether a *tmux-driven* interactive session still counts as interactive to
  Anthropic is unverified — run ``agent-warmup verify`` near a reset boundary and
  eyeball the captured /usage panel before trusting the recurring install.

Subcommands:
  run        Spawn interactive claude, send the warmup prompt, log the result.
  at         Queue a one-shot ``run`` via pueue (--at / --delay).
  install    Generate + load a recurring timer (macOS launchd / Linux systemd).
  uninstall  Unload + remove the recurring timer.
  status     Show pending one-shots, the installed timer, and recent run logs.
  cancel     Remove pending pueue one-shots.
  verify     run --verify --keep — the empirical experiment helper.

Run flags (shared by run / at / install):
  --model M     Claude model (default: $AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL or "haiku" — keeps
                window-token consumption tiny).
  --prompt P    Warmup prompt (default: a one-line "reply hi").
  --timeout S   Seconds to wait for a reply before giving up (default 120).
  --verify      After the reply, send /usage and capture the panel into the log.
  --keep        Do not kill the tmux session afterwards (for inspection).

Env:
  AGENT_WARMUP_SOCKET   tmux socket name (default: agent-warmup)
  AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL    default model (mirrors dot_config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh)

Cache / logs: $XDG_CACHE_HOME/agent-warmup/ (run-*.log, launchd/systemd output).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import getpass
import os
import plistlib
import shlex
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

GROUP = "agent-warmup"
LABEL_PREFIX = "agent-warmup:"
SOCKET = os.environ.get("AGENT_WARMUP_SOCKET", "agent-warmup")
LAUNCHD_LABEL = f"com.{getpass.getuser()}.agent-warmup"
SYSTEMD_UNIT = "agent-warmup"
DEFAULT_PROMPT = "Reply with just: hi"
DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 120
READY_TIMEOUT = 45
STABLE_SECS = 4.0

# Mirror scripts/fleet/exec.py:_PATH_PRELUDE so tmux/claude/pueue/launchctl are
# found in the minimal env launchd/systemd hand us (deliberately puts package
# manager dirs ahead of legacy ~/bin). Expanded and merged into PATH at startup.
_PATH_PRELUDE = [
    "~/.dotfiles/bin", "~/.cargo/bin", "~/.local/bin", "~/bin",
    "/opt/homebrew/bin", "/usr/local/bin", "/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin",
    "~/.linuxbrew/bin",
]


def _augment_path() -> None:
    extra = [str(Path(p).expanduser()) for p in _PATH_PRELUDE]
    current = os.environ.get("PATH", "").split(os.pathsep)
    merged = extra + [p for p in current if p and p not in extra]
    os.environ["PATH"] = os.pathsep.join(merged)


def cache_dir() -> Path:
    base = os.environ.get("XDG_CACHE_HOME") or str(Path.home() / ".cache")
    d = Path(base) / "agent-warmup"
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return d


def isolated_cwd() -> Path:
    d = cache_dir() / "claude"
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return d


def script_path() -> Path:
    override = os.environ.get("AGENT_WARMUP_SCRIPT")
    if override:
        return Path(override).expanduser()
    return Path(__file__).resolve()


def run(cmd: list[str], *, check: bool = False) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
    return subprocess.run(
        cmd, text=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, check=check
    )


def notify(title: str, message: str) -> None:
    """Best-effort desktop notification; always also echo to stderr."""
    print(f"{title}: {message}", file=sys.stderr)
    if sys.platform == "darwin" and shutil.which("osascript"):
        body = message.replace('"', "'")
        head = title.replace('"', "'")
        run(["osascript", "-e", f'display notification "{body}" with title "{head}"'])
    elif shutil.which("notify-send"):
        run(["notify-send", title, message])


# --- tmux helpers (dedicated socket) ----------------------------------------

def _tmux(*args: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
    return run(["tmux", "-L", SOCKET, *args])


def _session_alive(session: str) -> bool:
    return _tmux("has-session", "-t", session).returncode == 0


def _capture(session: str, lines: int = 200) -> str:
    cp = _tmux("capture-pane", "-p", "-S", f"-{lines}", "-t", session)
    return cp.stdout if cp.returncode == 0 else ""


def _send_text(session: str, text: str) -> None:
    # Clear any pre-filled input, type the text literally, pause, then submit.
    _tmux("send-keys", "-t", session, "C-u")
    _tmux("send-keys", "-t", session, "-l", text)
    time.sleep(0.4)
    _tmux("send-keys", "-t", session, "Enter")


# --- run --------------------------------------------------------------------

_TRUST_MARKERS = ("do you trust", "trust the files", "trust this folder")
_READY_MARKERS = ("for shortcuts", "? for", "› ", "│ >", "welcome to claude")
_AUTH_MARKERS = ("setup-token", "please run /login", "invalid api key", "authentication", "logged out")


def _wait_ready(session: str, deadline: float) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Wait for the claude TUI input box; accept a first-run folder-trust prompt."""
    trusted = False
    while time.time() < deadline:
        if not _session_alive(session):
            return False, _capture(session)
        text = _capture(session).lower()
        if not trusted and any(m in text for m in _TRUST_MARKERS):
            _tmux("send-keys", "-t", session, "Enter")
            trusted = True
            time.sleep(1.0)
            continue
        if any(m in text for m in _AUTH_MARKERS):
            return False, _capture(session)
        if any(m in text for m in _READY_MARKERS):
            return True, _capture(session)
        time.sleep(1.0)
    # Fall back to "probably ready" if the session is still alive after settling.
    return _session_alive(session), _capture(session)


def _wait_response(session: str, deadline: float) -> str:
    """Wait until the pane output stabilises (reply finished) or timeout."""
    last = ""
    last_change = time.time()
    while time.time() < deadline:
        if not _session_alive(session):
            break
        text = _capture(session)
        if text != last:
            last, last_change = text, time.time()
        elif time.time() - last_change >= STABLE_SECS:
            break
        time.sleep(1.0)
    return last


def cmd_run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    if not shutil.which("tmux"):
        notify("agent-warmup", "tmux not found on PATH; cannot warm up")
        return 127
    if not shutil.which("claude"):
        notify("agent-warmup", "claude CLI not found on PATH; cannot warm up")
        return 127

    ts = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")
    session = f"warmup-{ts}"
    log = cache_dir() / f"run-{ts}.log"
    cwd = isolated_cwd()
    model = args.model or os.environ.get("AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL") or "haiku"
    prompt = args.prompt or DEFAULT_PROMPT

    # Subscription auth only: an API key would route this to metered credit and
    # would NOT advance the 5-hour subscription window.
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.pop("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", None)

    # Reap any stale warmup sessions from a previous crashed run.
    for line in _tmux("list-sessions", "-F", "#{session_name}").stdout.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("warmup-") and line != session:
            _tmux("kill-session", "-t", line)

    started = datetime.now().astimezone()

    def write_log(status: str, capture: str, usage: str = "") -> None:
        with log.open("w") as fh:
            fh.write(f"# agent-warmup run {started.isoformat()}\n")
            fh.write(f"status: {status}\n")
            fh.write(f"model: {model}\n")
            fh.write(f"prompt: {prompt}\n")
            fh.write(f"session: {session} (socket {SOCKET})\n")
            fh.write(f"cwd: {cwd}\n")
            if usage:
                fh.write("\n## /usage panel\n")
                fh.write(usage)
                fh.write("\n")
            fh.write("\n## final pane capture\n")
            fh.write(capture)
            fh.write("\n")

    claude_cmd = f"exec claude --model {shlex.quote(model)}"
    cp = subprocess.run(
        ["tmux", "-L", SOCKET, "new-session", "-d", "-s", session, "-x", "200", "-y", "50",
         "-c", str(cwd), claude_cmd],
        text=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=env,
    )
    if cp.returncode != 0:
        write_log("error: tmux new-session failed", cp.stderr or cp.stdout)
        notify("agent-warmup", f"failed to spawn claude session: {cp.stderr.strip()}")
        return 1

    ready, capture = _wait_ready(session, time.time() + READY_TIMEOUT)
    if not ready:
        write_log("error: claude not ready / auth required", capture)
        if not args.keep:
            _tmux("kill-session", "-t", session)
        notify("agent-warmup", "claude did not become ready (auth or startup issue) — check the log")
        print(f"agent-warmup: not ready; log {log}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    _send_text(session, prompt)
    capture = _wait_response(session, time.time() + args.timeout)

    usage = ""
    if args.verify:
        _send_text(session, "/usage")
        time.sleep(2.0)
        usage = _wait_response(session, time.time() + 30)

    write_log("ok", capture, usage)
    if not args.keep:
        _tmux("kill-session", "-t", session)
        print(f"agent-warmup: warmup sent; log {log}")
    else:
        print(f"agent-warmup: warmup sent; session kept ({session}); log {log}")
        print(f"  attach with: tmux -L {SOCKET} attach -t {session}")
    return 0


# --- pueue one-shot ---------------------------------------------------------

def _run_argv(args: argparse.Namespace) -> list[str]:
    """Reconstruct a `run` invocation from shared run flags."""
    argv = [str(script_path()), "run"]
    if args.model:
        argv += ["--model", args.model]
    if args.prompt:
        argv += ["--prompt", args.prompt]
    if args.timeout != DEFAULT_TIMEOUT:
        argv += ["--timeout", str(args.timeout)]
    if getattr(args, "verify", False):
        argv.append("--verify")
    return argv


def _ensure_group() -> None:
    run(["pueue", "group", "add", GROUP])
    run(["pueue", "parallel", "-g", GROUP, "1"])


def cmd_at(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    if not shutil.which("pueue"):
        print("agent-warmup: pueue not installed", file=sys.stderr)
        return 127
    if not args.at and not args.delay:
        print("agent-warmup at: pass --at or --delay", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    delay = args.delay or args.at
    command = " ".join(shlex.quote(p) for p in _run_argv(args))
    label = f"{LABEL_PREFIX}oneshot:{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')}"
    if args.dry_run:
        print(f"pueue add -g {GROUP} --label {shlex.quote(label)} "
              f"--delay {shlex.quote(delay)} {shlex.quote(command)}")
        return 0
    _ensure_group()
    cp = run(["pueue", "add", "-g", GROUP, "--label", label,
              "--delay", delay, "--print-task-id", command])
    if cp.returncode != 0:
        print(cp.stderr or cp.stdout, file=sys.stderr, end="")
        return cp.returncode
    print(f"scheduled {label} at {delay} (task {cp.stdout.strip()})")
    return 0


def _pueue_oneshots() -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:
    """Return (task_id, status, label) for pending agent-warmup one-shots."""
    import json
    if not shutil.which("pueue"):
        return []
    cp = run(["pueue", "status", "--json"])
    if cp.returncode != 0:
        return []
    try:
        data = json.loads(cp.stdout)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return []
    out = []
    for tid, task in (data.get("tasks") or {}).items():
        if not isinstance(task, dict):
            continue
        label = str(task.get("label") or "")
        if not label.startswith(LABEL_PREFIX):
            continue
        status = task.get("status")
        name = next(iter(status)) if isinstance(status, dict) and status else str(status)
        if name == "Done":
            continue
        out.append((str(task.get("id", tid)), name, label))
    return out


def cmd_cancel(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    tasks = _pueue_oneshots()
    if not tasks:
        print("no pending agent-warmup one-shots")
        return 0
    for tid, _status, label in tasks:
        cp = run(["pueue", "remove", tid])
        if cp.returncode != 0:
            run(["pueue", "kill", tid])
            cp = run(["pueue", "remove", tid])
        print(f"removed task {tid} ({label})" if cp.returncode == 0
              else (cp.stderr or cp.stdout))
    return 0


# --- recurring timer install ------------------------------------------------

_WEEKDAY_NAMES = {
    "mon": 1, "tue": 2, "wed": 3, "thu": 4, "fri": 5, "sat": 6, "sun": 0,
}
_SYSTEMD_DAY = {1: "Mon", 2: "Tue", 3: "Wed", 4: "Thu", 5: "Fri", 6: "Sat", 0: "Sun"}


def _parse_days(spec: str) -> list[int]:
    """Return launchd Weekday integers (Sun=0..Sat=6). Empty list = every day."""
    spec = (spec or "daily").strip().lower()
    if spec in ("daily", "everyday", "all"):
        return []
    if spec == "weekdays":
        return [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
    if spec == "weekends":
        return [0, 6]
    days = []
    for tok in re.split(r"[,\s]+", spec):
        if tok[:3] in _WEEKDAY_NAMES:
            days.append(_WEEKDAY_NAMES[tok[:3]])
    return sorted(set(days))


def _parse_hhmm(s: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    m = re.fullmatch(r"(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})", s.strip())
    if not m:
        raise SystemExit(f"agent-warmup install: bad --time {s!r} (want HH:MM)")
    hh, mm = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))
    if hh > 23 or mm > 59:
        raise SystemExit(f"agent-warmup install: time out of range {s!r}")
    return hh, mm


def _launchd_plist_path() -> Path:
    return Path.home() / "Library" / "LaunchAgents" / f"{LAUNCHD_LABEL}.plist"


def _install_launchd(args: argparse.Namespace, days: list[int], hh: int, mm: int) -> int:
    program = _run_argv(args)
    if days:
        cal = [{"Weekday": d, "Hour": hh, "Minute": mm} for d in days]
    else:
        cal = {"Hour": hh, "Minute": mm}
    plist = {
        "Label": LAUNCHD_LABEL,
        "ProgramArguments": program,
        "StartCalendarInterval": cal,
        "EnvironmentVariables": {"PATH": os.environ["PATH"]},
        "StandardOutPath": str(cache_dir() / "launchd.out.log"),
        "StandardErrorPath": str(cache_dir() / "launchd.err.log"),
        "RunAtLoad": False,
    }
    path = _launchd_plist_path()
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with path.open("wb") as fh:
        plistlib.dump(plist, fh)
    # Validate with the platform tool (repo invariant: validate config with the app).
    if shutil.which("plutil"):
        cp = run(["plutil", "-lint", str(path)])
        if cp.returncode != 0:
            print(cp.stdout or cp.stderr, file=sys.stderr, end="")
            return 1
    uid = os.getuid()
    run(["launchctl", "bootout", f"gui/{uid}/{LAUNCHD_LABEL}"])
    cp = run(["launchctl", "bootstrap", f"gui/{uid}", str(path)])
    if cp.returncode != 0:
        # Older macOS fallback.
        run(["launchctl", "unload", str(path)])
        cp = run(["launchctl", "load", "-w", str(path)])
    if cp.returncode != 0:
        print(cp.stderr or cp.stdout, file=sys.stderr, end="")
        return cp.returncode
    print(f"installed launchd agent {LAUNCHD_LABEL} → {path}")
    return 0


def _systemd_dir() -> Path:
    base = os.environ.get("XDG_CONFIG_HOME") or str(Path.home() / ".config")
    d = Path(base) / "systemd" / "user"
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return d


def _install_systemd(args: argparse.Namespace, days: list[int], hh: int, mm: int) -> int:
    program = " ".join(shlex.quote(p) for p in _run_argv(args))
    if days:
        names = ",".join(_SYSTEMD_DAY[d] for d in sorted(days))
        oncal = f"{names} *-*-* {hh:02d}:{mm:02d}:00"
    else:
        oncal = f"*-*-* {hh:02d}:{mm:02d}:00"
    d = _systemd_dir()
    (d / f"{SYSTEMD_UNIT}.service").write_text(
        "[Unit]\n"
        "Description=Claude quota-window warmup\n\n"
        "[Service]\n"
        "Type=oneshot\n"
        f"ExecStart={program}\n"
    )
    (d / f"{SYSTEMD_UNIT}.timer").write_text(
        "[Unit]\n"
        "Description=Claude quota-window warmup timer\n\n"
        "[Timer]\n"
        f"OnCalendar={oncal}\n"
        "Persistent=true\n\n"
        "[Install]\n"
        "WantedBy=timers.target\n"
    )
    if shutil.which("systemd-analyze"):
        cp = run(["systemd-analyze", "verify", str(d / f"{SYSTEMD_UNIT}.timer")])
        if cp.returncode != 0:
            print(cp.stderr or cp.stdout, file=sys.stderr, end="")
            return 1
    run(["systemctl", "--user", "daemon-reload"])
    cp = run(["systemctl", "--user", "enable", "--now", f"{SYSTEMD_UNIT}.timer"])
    if cp.returncode != 0:
        print(cp.stderr or cp.stdout, file=sys.stderr, end="")
        return cp.returncode
    print(f"installed systemd user timer {SYSTEMD_UNIT}.timer (OnCalendar={oncal})")
    return 0


def cmd_install(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    days = _parse_days(args.daily)
    hh, mm = _parse_hhmm(args.time)
    if sys.platform == "darwin":
        return _install_launchd(args, days, hh, mm)
    return _install_systemd(args, days, hh, mm)


def cmd_uninstall(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    if sys.platform == "darwin":
        uid = os.getuid()
        run(["launchctl", "bootout", f"gui/{uid}/{LAUNCHD_LABEL}"])
        path = _launchd_plist_path()
        run(["launchctl", "unload", str(path)])
        if path.exists():
            path.unlink()
            print(f"removed launchd agent {LAUNCHD_LABEL}")
        else:
            print("no launchd agent installed")
        return 0
    run(["systemctl", "--user", "disable", "--now", f"{SYSTEMD_UNIT}.timer"])
    d = _systemd_dir()
    removed = False
    for name in (f"{SYSTEMD_UNIT}.timer", f"{SYSTEMD_UNIT}.service"):
        f = d / name
        if f.exists():
            f.unlink()
            removed = True
    run(["systemctl", "--user", "daemon-reload"])
    print("removed systemd user timer" if removed else "no systemd timer installed")
    return 0


# --- status -----------------------------------------------------------------

def _timer_state() -> str:
    if sys.platform == "darwin":
        path = _launchd_plist_path()
        if not path.exists():
            return "not installed"
        uid = os.getuid()
        cp = run(["launchctl", "print", f"gui/{uid}/{LAUNCHD_LABEL}"])
        return f"launchd {LAUNCHD_LABEL} ({'loaded' if cp.returncode == 0 else 'present, not loaded'})"
    if not (_systemd_dir() / f"{SYSTEMD_UNIT}.timer").exists():
        return "not installed"
    cp = run(["systemctl", "--user", "list-timers", "--no-pager", f"{SYSTEMD_UNIT}.timer"])
    next_line = ""
    for line in cp.stdout.splitlines():
        if SYSTEMD_UNIT in line:
            next_line = line.strip()
    return f"systemd {SYSTEMD_UNIT}.timer ({next_line or 'enabled'})"


def _recent_runs(limit: int = 5) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    logs = sorted(cache_dir().glob("run-*.log"), reverse=True)[:limit]
    out = []
    for log in logs:
        status = "?"
        for line in log.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
            if line.startswith("status:"):
                status = line.split(":", 1)[1].strip()
                break
        out.append((log.name, status))
    return out


def cmd_status(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    if args.json:
        import json
        print(json.dumps({
            "timer": _timer_state(),
            "oneshots": [{"task_id": t, "status": s, "label": l} for t, s, l in _pueue_oneshots()],
            "recent_runs": [{"log": n, "status": s} for n, s in _recent_runs()],
        }, indent=2))
        return 0
    print(f"timer:    {_timer_state()}")
    oneshots = _pueue_oneshots()
    print(f"oneshots: {len(oneshots)} pending")
    for tid, status, label in oneshots:
        print(f"  task {tid}  {status}  {label}")
    runs = _recent_runs()
    print(f"recent:   {len(runs)} run log(s) in {cache_dir()}")
    for name, status in runs:
        print(f"  {name}  status={status}")
    return 0


# --- arg parsing ------------------------------------------------------------

import re  # noqa: E402  (used by _parse_days / _parse_hhmm)


def _add_run_flags(p: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> None:
    p.add_argument("--model", help="Claude model (default $AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL or haiku)")
    p.add_argument("--prompt", help=f"Warmup prompt (default: {DEFAULT_PROMPT!r})")
    p.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT, help="Reply wait seconds")
    p.add_argument("--verify", action="store_true", help="Send /usage and capture the panel")


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="agent-warmup", description=__doc__,
                                formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=False)

    s = sub.add_parser("run", help="Spawn interactive claude and send the warmup prompt")
    _add_run_flags(s)
    s.add_argument("--keep", action="store_true", help="Keep the tmux session afterwards")
    s.set_defaults(func=cmd_run)

    s = sub.add_parser("at", help="Queue a one-shot run via pueue")
    s.add_argument("--at", help="Absolute time for pueue --delay (e.g. '06:00', 'tomorrow 06:00')")
    s.add_argument("--delay", help="Relative delay for pueue --delay (e.g. 8h, 30m)")
    s.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    _add_run_flags(s)
    s.set_defaults(func=cmd_at)

    s = sub.add_parser("install", help="Install a recurring launchd/systemd timer")
    s.add_argument("--daily", default="weekdays",
                   help="daily | weekdays | weekends | comma list (mon,wed,fri)")
    s.add_argument("--time", default="06:00", help="HH:MM (24h)")
    _add_run_flags(s)
    s.set_defaults(func=cmd_install)

    s = sub.add_parser("uninstall", help="Remove the recurring timer")
    s.set_defaults(func=cmd_uninstall)

    s = sub.add_parser("status", help="Show timer, pending one-shots, recent runs")
    s.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    s.set_defaults(func=cmd_status)

    s = sub.add_parser("cancel", help="Remove pending pueue one-shots")
    s.set_defaults(func=cmd_cancel)

    s = sub.add_parser("verify", help="run --verify --keep (empirical experiment helper)")
    _add_run_flags(s)
    s.set_defaults(func=lambda a: cmd_run(argparse.Namespace(
        **{**vars(a), "keep": True, "verify": True})))

    return p


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    _augment_path()
    parser = build_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if not hasattr(args, "func"):
        parser.print_help()
        return 0
    return int(args.func(args))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

```zsh
# 49_agent_warmup_completion.zsh - tab completion for `agent-warmup`.
# Source CLI: dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_agent-warmup (argparse, subcommands).
# Keep in sync with dot_config/bash/49_agent_warmup_completion.bash.

(( $+commands[agent-warmup] )) || return 0

_agent_warmup() {
    local context state state_descr line
    typeset -A opt_args

    local -a run_flags=(
        '--model[Claude model (default $AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL or haiku)]:model:(haiku sonnet opus)'
        '--prompt[warmup prompt]:prompt:'
        '--timeout[reply wait seconds]:seconds:'
        '--verify[send /usage and capture the panel]'
    )

    _arguments -C \
        '(- *)'{-h,--help}'[show help]' \
        '1:command:->command' \
        '*::arg:->args'

    case "$state" in
        command)
            local -a cmds=(
                'run:spawn interactive claude and send the warmup prompt'
                'at:queue a one-shot run via pueue'
                'install:install a recurring launchd/systemd timer'
                'uninstall:remove the recurring timer'
                'status:show timer, pending one-shots, recent runs'
                'cancel:remove pending pueue one-shots'
                'verify:run --verify --keep (empirical experiment helper)'
            )
            _describe -t commands 'agent-warmup command' cmds
            ;;
        args)
            case "$line[1]" in
                run)
                    _arguments $run_flags '--keep[keep the tmux session afterwards]'
                    ;;
                at)
                    _arguments $run_flags \
                        '--at[absolute time for pueue --delay]:time:' \
                        '--delay[relative delay for pueue --delay, e.g. 8h]:delay:' \
                        '--dry-run[print the pueue command only]'
                    ;;
                install)
                    _arguments $run_flags \
                        '--daily[schedule]:schedule:(daily weekdays weekends)' \
                        '--time[HH:MM 24h]:time:'
                    ;;
                verify)
                    _arguments $run_flags
                    ;;
                status)
                    _arguments '--json[machine-readable output]'
                    ;;
            esac
            ;;
    esac
}
```
