# 49_agent_warmup_completion.bash - tab completion for `agent-warmup`.
# Source CLI: dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_agent-warmup (argparse, subcommands).
# Keep in sync with dot_config/zsh/tools/49_agent_warmup_completion.zsh.

command -v agent-warmup >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0

_agent_warmup_completion() {
    local cur prev words cword
    _init_completion || return

    local cmds="run at install uninstall status cancel verify"
    local run_flags="--model --prompt --timeout --verify"

    # Find the subcommand (first non-flag word after argv[0]).
    local i sub=""
    for ((i = 1; i < cword; i++)); do
        case "${words[i]}" in
            -*) ;;
            *) sub="${words[i]}"; break ;;
        esac
    done

    if [ -z "$sub" ]; then
        COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$cmds -h --help" -- "$cur") )
        return
    fi

    case "$prev" in
        --model) COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "haiku sonnet opus" -- "$cur") ); return ;;
        --daily) COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "daily weekdays weekends" -- "$cur") ); return ;;
        --prompt|--timeout|--time|--at|--delay) return ;;
    esac

    local opts=""
    case "$sub" in
        run)    opts="$run_flags --keep" ;;
        at)     opts="$run_flags --at --delay --dry-run" ;;
        install) opts="$run_flags --daily --time" ;;
        verify) opts="$run_flags" ;;
        status) opts="--json" ;;
    esac
    [ -n "$opts" ] && COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "$opts" -- "$cur") )
}

complete -F _agent_warmup_completion agent-warmup

```md
# Agent quota warmup (`agent-warmup`)

`agent-warmup` starts the **Claude Pro/Max 5-hour subscription usage window** at
a scheduled time (e.g. 06:00 on workdays), so a fresh window is already running
before you begin real work — plus an ad-hoc "warm up at this time" one-shot.

The CLI lives at `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_agent-warmup` (deployed to
`~/.dotfiles/bin/agent-warmup`, on `PATH`). Claude-only by design — Codex /
OpenCode have different quota systems.

## Why it drives an interactive session (not `claude -p`)

!!! warning "The 2026-06-15 billing split changed everything"
    Since **2026-06-15**, only **interactive** Claude Code usage advances the
    rolling 5-hour subscription window. **Headless `claude -p`** (and the Agent
    SDK, GitHub Actions, third-party agents) now draws from a separate metered
    *Agent SDK credit* pool — it does **not** move the window. A `claude -p`
    "warmup" would silently burn metered API credit and accomplish nothing.
    See [pitfalls/headless-claude-p-does-not-move-5h-window.md](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/headless-claude-p-does-not-move-5h-window.md).

So `agent-warmup run` drives a **real interactive `claude` TUI**:

1. spawns a detached tmux session on a dedicated socket (`tmux -L agent-warmup`);
2. in an isolated cwd (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME/agent-warmup/claude`) so no project
   `CLAUDE.md` / context is loaded;
3. with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` unset so it uses your **subscription** auth (an API
   key would route to metered credit and not move the window);
4. accepts the first-run folder-trust prompt, sends a tiny prompt + Enter, waits
   for the reply, logs it, then kills the session (unless `--keep`).

Default model is `$AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL` (→ `haiku`) to keep window-token
consumption tiny.

!!! note "Unverified assumption — confirm empirically"
    Whether Anthropic still classifies a *tmux-driven* interactive session as
    "interactive" is unconfirmed. The billing system most likely keys off
    client/session **type**, not who physically pressed Enter — but run
    `agent-warmup verify` near a reset boundary and eyeball the captured
    `/usage` panel **before** trusting the recurring install.

## Commands

\```bash
# One-off: warm up now, keep the session + capture /usage for inspection
agent-warmup verify

# Recurring: 06:00 every weekday (launchd on macOS, systemd user timer on Linux)
agent-warmup install --daily weekdays --time 06:00
agent-warmup uninstall

# Ad-hoc one-shot via pueue
agent-warmup at --at '06:00'
agent-warmup at --delay 8h

# Inspection
agent-warmup status            # timer state + pending one-shots + recent run logs
agent-warmup status --json
agent-warmup cancel            # remove pending one-shots

# The primitive the schedulers call
agent-warmup run [--model haiku] [--prompt 'Reply with just: hi'] [--timeout 120] [--keep] [--verify]
\```

`at` and `install` forward the shared run flags (`--model`, `--prompt`,
`--timeout`, `--verify`) into the scheduled `run`.

## Backends

| Schedule | macOS | Linux |
|---|---|---|
| Recurring (`install`) | `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.<user>.agent-warmup.plist` (`StartCalendarInterval`), loaded with `launchctl bootstrap`; validated with `plutil -lint` | `~/.config/systemd/user/agent-warmup.{service,timer}` (`OnCalendar=`, `Persistent=true`), `systemctl --user enable --now`; validated with `systemd-analyze verify` |
| One-shot (`at`) | pueue group `agent-warmup`, label `agent-warmup:oneshot:<ts>` | same |

The recurring timer is **imperative and opt-in** — generated by `install`, it is
*not* chezmoi-managed (so there is no `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` prompt and no forced
install on every machine). Run `install` on the host where you want the warmup.

## Caveats

- **Machine asleep at the scheduled time** → the job fires on wake (launchd
  coalesces missed calendar events; systemd uses `Persistent=true`), so the
  window geometry shifts to wake time.
- **Keychain must be unlocked** (you must be logged into the GUI session) for
  subscription auth to work from launchd/systemd.
- **Auth expiry** → if the session can't authenticate, `run` logs the capture
  and fires a desktop notification rather than typing into a dead session.

## Relationship to `agent-wakeup`

`agent-warmup` is a **separate** tool from
[`agent-wakeup`](agent-panes-discovery.md) (quota *recovery* — scheduling a
`continue` into an existing blocked pane). Warmup needs no existing pane, starts
a fresh isolated session, and must not continue real work. The broader
auto-continue loop and a unified dashboard remain backlog items.

```md
# Headless `claude -p` warmup does not start the 5-hour subscription window

**Symptoms** (grep this section): a scheduled `claude -p 'Reply: hi'` "warmup"
job runs cleanly (exit 0, a reply in the log) but the Claude Pro/Max **5-hour
usage window never starts** — `/usage` in interactive Claude Code still shows no
active session window at the warmup time; the window only begins later when you
actually start typing interactively; metered **Agent SDK credit** is consumed
instead of subscription usage; "warmup at 06:00" has no effect on when your
interactive window resets.
**First seen**: 2026-06-20 (designing `agent-warmup`)
**Affects**: any automation that assumes headless `claude -p` / Agent SDK runs
count toward the interactive subscription 5-hour window
**Status**: by design (Anthropic billing change) — `agent-warmup` works around it
by driving an interactive TUI instead

## Symptom

The "obvious" warmup — run a tiny prompt headlessly from launchd/cron/pueue so
the 5-hour window is already running before you start work:

\```bash
cd ~/.cache/agent-warmup && claude -p 'Reply exactly: hi'
\```

…succeeds but does **nothing** to the interactive window. You burn metered API
credit and the window still starts whenever you first type interactively.

## Root cause

As of **2026-06-15**, Anthropic split billing:

- **Interactive** Claude.ai chat and **interactive terminal Claude Code** stay on
  the subscription and advance the rolling **5-hour window**.
- **Non-interactive** usage — the **Agent SDK**, the **headless `claude`
  command** (`claude -p`), Claude Code **GitHub Actions**, and third-party agents
  authenticating with your subscription — now draws from a **separate monthly
  metered credit pool** (~$20 Pro / $100 Max5x / $200 Max20x, API rates, no
  rollover).

Anthropic's framing: *"if a human presses enter, you stay on your subscription;
if a robot presses enter while you're away, that usage moves to the new metered
credit."* The 5-hour window is **only** moved by interactive usage.

Compounding trap: `--bare` (the clean way to skip `CLAUDE.md`) explicitly does
**not** read the subscription OAuth token — it forces `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. So
`claude --bare -p …` is doubly wrong for warmup (API billing, never subscription).

## Fix / workaround

To move the window you must drive a **genuine interactive Claude Code session**.
`agent-warmup run` (see [docs/tools/agent-warmup.md](../docs/tools/agent-warmup.md))
does this:

- spawn a detached tmux session (`tmux -L agent-warmup`) running interactive
  `claude` in an isolated cwd;
- `unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` so it uses subscription auth (do **not** use
  `--bare`);
- `tmux send-keys` a tiny prompt + Enter.

## Verify

The interactive-via-tmux classification is **not documented** — confirm it
empirically near a reset boundary before trusting recurring scheduling:

\```bash
agent-warmup verify   # run --verify --keep: sends /usage, keeps the session
tmux -L agent-warmup attach -t warmup-<ts>   # eyeball the /usage panel
\```

Check whether a new 5-hour session window started. If it did **not**, the
tmux-driven session is also being classified as non-interactive — stop and
rethink (there may be no automatable way to warm the window).

## References

- Billing split explainer: <https://www.pravinkumar.co/blog/claude-june-15-billing-change-explained-2026>
- [docs/tools/agent-warmup.md](../docs/tools/agent-warmup.md)
- [backlog/agent-quota-warmup-at-time.md](../backlog/agent-quota-warmup-at-time.md)
- Related stale-HUD trap: [claude-hud-usage-statusline-stale.md](claude-hud-usage-statusline-stale.md)

Done. Everything is built, verified, committed, and deployed.

## Summary

I evaluated your need and found the original premise was broken by a recent billing change — then pivoted the design with you and shipped it.

### The key finding (why your instinct to "verify" was right)
Web research confirmed the **2026-06-15 Anthropic billing split**: headless `claude -p` (and the Agent SDK) now draw from a *separate metered credit pool* and **no longer move the interactive 5-hour subscription window** — only genuine interactive Claude Code does. The backlog's original "isolated cwd + `claude -p`" warmup would have silently burned API credit and accomplished nothing. So warmup must drive a **real interactive `claude` TUI**.

### What shipped — `agent-warmup` (2 commits on `main`)
**`feat(agent)`** — new CLI `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_agent-warmup`:
- `run` spawns interactive `claude` in a **detached tmux session** (dedicated socket `tmux -L agent-warmup`, isolated cwd, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` unset for subscription auth, `--model haiku`), handles the folder-trust prompt, sends a tiny prompt + Enter, logs + desktop-notifies on failure.
- `at` → pueue one-shot; `install`/`uninstall` → recurring **launchd** (macOS) / **systemd user timer** (Linux), opt-in/imperative; `status`/`cancel`; `verify` (the empirical experiment helper).
- zsh+bash completions, `docs/tools/agent-warmup.md` + nav, a symptom-titled pitfall, backlog + TODO marked shipped.

**`fix(agent)`** — the code-quality cleanups you asked for on Codex's `agent-wakeup`: word-boundary-anchored quota regex, self-contained HUD detection (dropped the brittle post-hoc string checks), documented the full-text-vs-tail asymmetry, and a shell empty-path guard. Conventional messages with the `Co-Authored-By` footer.

### Verified (zero quota consumed)
Install → `plutil -lint` → loaded → `status` → uninstall round-trip; pueue add/cancel; completions parse in both shells; regex unit tests; agent-wakeup syntax. mkdocs `--strict` still fails **only** on pre-existing `llmstxt`/i18n drift and a stale `import_ssh_to_bw.sh.md` nav ref — my page builds cleanly and adds zero new warnings.

### Your turn — the one thing I deliberately did *not* run
The live warmup consumes your subscription window, so I left it for you. Near a reset boundary:

```bash
agent-warmup verify                          # keeps the session, captures /usage
tmux -L agent-warmup attach -t warmup-<ts>   # eyeball whether a new 5h window started
```

If `/usage` confirms a new window started, the tmux-interactive approach works → `agent-warmup install --daily weekdays --time 06:00`. If it doesn't, the pitfall and docs both flag that there may be no automatable way to warm the window, and we'd revisit.

One scope note: per your steer, I kept this **standalone** — the auto-continue loop, the cross-agent delayed-run scheduler, and the unified dashboard-TUI remain separate backlog items.

## 還沒驗證的有兩件事

**1. 工具本身的「活體」運作(機械層面)**
我測完了所有**排程路徑**(install→plutil→load→uninstall、pueue at/cancel、status、補全),但**從來沒有真的讓它跑起一個 claude 互動 session**過 —— 因為那會消耗你的額度、啟動你的視窗,我不該擅自做。

所以 `run` 裡這幾個**啟發式**還沒在真實 TUI 上驗證過:
- `_wait_ready` 能不能正確判斷 claude 輸入框就緒
- 首次資料夾的 trust 提示("Do you trust the files…")能不能被自動按 Enter 接受
- 送出 prompt 後的「回覆完成」偵測

這些是我唯一沒辦法在不花額度下測的東西。**建議今晚先手動跑一次** `agent-warmup verify`(它會保留 session 讓你看),確認機制真的能驅動 claude,再交給 5 點的排程 —— 否則萬一 5 點那次是「史上第一次活體執行」就掛了,白白浪費一個早上。

**2. 它到底會不會推動 5h 視窗(計費分類問題)**
這就是你說的「verify til midnight」那件事 —— tmux 驅動的互動 session 會不會被 Anthropic 算成 interactive。這個**只能靠早上那次測試**回答。

## 明天早上 5 點測試:可以,但有前提

```bash
# 方式 A:裝成 5:00 的循環 timer(--verify 讓早上的 log 自動抓 /usage)
agent-warmup install --daily daily --time 05:00 --verify

# 方式 B:只測一次,用 pueue 排到明早 5:00
agent-warmup at --at '05:00' --verify
```

早上起來看結果:
```bash
agent-warmup status                 # 看有沒有跑過
cat ~/.cache/agent-warmup/run-*.log # --verify 會把 /usage 面板存進去
# 對照面板裡的 5h session 是不是 ~05:00 才開始 → 答案就出來了
```

**務必注意的坑:**
- **機器不能睡著**。macOS launchd 的 `StartCalendarInterval` 在睡眠時不會準點觸發,要等喚醒才補跑。想要準 5 點觸發,前一晚先 `caffeinate -s` 或用 `pmset` 排一個喚醒,否則它會在你早上開機/喚醒時才跑(那也能驗證視窗,只是時間點不是 5:00)。
- **鑰匙圈要解鎖**(你得在登入狀態),否則訂閱認證在背景跑不起來。
- 想讓 5 點那次乾淨地證明「是它觸發的」,**前一晚別在午夜後用 claude**,確保 5 點前視窗是空的。

## 我的建議順序
1. **今晚**手動 `agent-warmup verify` → 確認活體機制 OK(花費極小)。
2. OK 的話再 `agent-warmup install --daily daily --time 05:00 --verify` + `caffeinate -s`。
3. 早上讀 log 的 `/usage` 面板 → 確認視窗是否真的在 5 點被推動。
4. 確認有效 → 改成 `--daily weekdays`;若無效 → pitfall 跟 docs 都已標註「可能無法自動暖機」,我們再回頭想別的辦法。

要不要我**現在就幫你跑一次 `agent-warmup verify`** 做機制驗證?(它會真的開一個 claude session、送一句 "hi"、保留 session 讓你 attach 檢查 —— 會用掉一點點額度並啟動你現在的 5h 視窗,所以由你決定。)

## 🔑 關於 5h 視窗 —— 強烈正面訊號,但還差最後一哩

`/usage` 面板顯示:
```
Haiku 4.5 · Claude Max · trader3206@gmail.com's Organization   ← 是訂閱(Max),不是 API
Current session  ███ 46% used · Resets 3:39am                  ← 這就是 5h 訂閱視窗
...
Usage credits are off · /usage-credits to turn them on         ← 計量 Agent SDK 額度池「沒開」
```

三個關鍵點:
1. 這個 tmux session 被認成 **Claude Max 訂閱** session,不是 API。
2. 用量被算進 **"Current session"(就是那個 5h 視窗)**,不是算進獨立的計量額度。
3. 底部的 **"Usage credits OFF"** —— 就是那個 June-15 之後的計量 Agent SDK 池,它沒被動到。

→ **這幾乎證實了:tmux 驅動的互動 claude 會被算成 interactive 訂閱用量、會推動 5h 視窗。** pitfall 裡那個「不確定」的假設,目前看是**成立(正面)**的。

**唯一還沒 100% 證實的**:這次視窗**本來就已經開著**(顯示 Resets 3:39am → 代表它約在昨晚 10:39pm 就啟動了),所以這次是「**加入**既有視窗」,沒能證明它能從**冷狀態啟動一個全新視窗**。

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-19 22:34:41Z)**_

Root cause nailed: **pid 25561 is `uv` itself — hung with no python child, holding only the launchd log fds.** `uv run --script` (the shebang launcher) wedged under launchd's context *before* it ever started python (the sample shows it stuck in `_pthread_join`, no tmux socket, no lock held). So:

- ✅ launchd fired exactly at 05:00, `caffeinate` kept the machine awake
- ❌ the **`uv run` launcher hung under launchd** → python never ran → no tmux session, no log, no notification, job "running" forever
- ⚠️ a contributing mess: my 03:00 `--keep` test left a tmux server + idle claude lingering on the socket

The cold-start question is therefore **still unanswered** — but I found a real unattended-mode bug. Let me clean up the wedged state first (safe — only touches the dedicated `agent-warmup` socket and the stuck job, never your main tmux):

While waiting, here's where we are so the context is clear:

## What happened with the 05:00 test
- ✅ **launchd fired exactly at 05:00**, `caffeinate` kept the machine awake — the scheduling layer works.
- ❌ **The `uv run` shebang launcher hung under launchd** (pid was `uv` itself, stuck before Python even started, no tmux session, no log, "running" for 1.5h). This is the real bug — and it means the cold-start window question is *still unanswered*.

## The fix I just shipped (pending this test)
1. **Scheduled runs now invoke the uv-env Python directly** (`[python3, script, run, …]`), bypassing the uv launcher that hung. Safe because the script is stdlib-only.
2. **Per-run unique tmux socket** + **`finally` cleanup** → a leftover `--keep` session or wedged run can never block a later one.
3. **Timeouts on every subprocess call** → a hung `tmux`/`claude` can no longer wedge the run forever; it bounds, logs, and notifies instead.

This 06:41 test verifies both the uv-hang fix *and* the still-unproven question of whether interactive `claude` even works under launchd's context.

A scheduled 05:00 launchd warmup wedged for 1.5h with no log and no exit. Root
cause: the `uv run` shebang launcher hangs under launchd's bootstrap context
before Python even starts. Fixes:

- Scheduled entrypoints (pueue / launchd / systemd) now invoke the resolved
  Python interpreter directly on the script (sys.executable, the uv-built env's
  python) instead of via the `uv run` shebang. Safe — the script is
  stdlib-only (dependencies = []).
- Every tmux subprocess call now has a timeout; a hung tmux server can no
  longer wedge the run forever.
- Per-run unique tmux socket (agent-warmup-<ts>) so a leftover `--keep`
  session or a wedged prior run can never block a later unattended run.
- run() wraps its body in try/finally and kills the per-run socket's server on
  exit (unless --keep), guaranteeing cleanup on every path.

Verified: attended `verify` still works end-to-end (per-run socket, status ok,
/usage captured) and is still interactive subscription usage (Claude Max,
"Current session" bucket, usage-credits off). NOTE: launchd execution surfaced
a second, deeper hang (Python stalls in dyld mapFileReadOnly under the gui
LaunchAgent bootstrap before claude launches) — tracked in the pitfall; the
recurring backend on macOS should prefer pueue (pueued runs in the user session,
not a gui LaunchAgent).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
echo "rc=$?"; git log --oneline -1
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-19 23:17:39Z)**_

**Found the real root cause.** `lsof` shows the uv-managed Python lives on a **secondary volume**: `/Volumes/Data/caches/uv-share/python/cpython-3.11.11.../python3.11` (device `1,29`, vs main `1,15`). Under a daemon (launchd/pueue) bootstrap, memory-mapping `.so` files from that volume **blocks in dyld** — likely a TCC/volume-access gate that only the GUI session has. That's why the attended path works but every daemon hangs. And it's why my earlier probe showed **Homebrew python (`/opt/homebrew/bin/python3`, on the main volume) completed under pueue** while the uv python hung.

The fix: scheduled runs must use a **main-volume Python**, not the uv interpreter on `/Volumes/Data`:

```md
# agent-warmup scheduled run hangs, exits early, or leaves a blank pane under launchd/pueue

**Symptoms** (grep this section): a launchd / pueue / systemd-scheduled `agent-warmup run`
wedges for hours with `state = running` / `last exit code = (never exited)` and
no run log; OR completes (exit 0) but the run log's `## /usage panel` and
`## final pane capture` are EMPTY; OR `pueue status` shows the task stuck on
`Running`; `sample <pid>` shows the process pinned in
`dyld4::SyscallDelegate::mapFileReadOnly` / `withReadOnlyMappedFile`; the stuck
process is `uv` (no Python child) or `python3 .../agent-warmup run`; the warmup's
tmux session exists but `tmux capture-pane` returns only blank lines; the exact
same `agent-warmup verify` works perfectly when run by hand in a terminal.
**First seen**: 2026-06-20 (bringing up `agent-warmup` on a Mac mini)
**Affects**: macOS background launch contexts (launchd `gui/uid` agents, `pueued`
daemon) spawning an interactive `claude` TUI. Likely any tool launching a fresh
GUI-bound TUI from a daemon bootstrap.
**Status**: fixed in `agent-warmup` (four stacked fixes below)

## Four stacked traps, each masking the next

Debugging found FOUR separate failures, only visible one at a time:

1. **`uv run` shebang hangs under launchd.** The first scheduled run wedged in
   the `uv` launcher itself (the stuck PID was `uv`, no Python child, stuck in
   dyld) before Python started — no session, no log, no exit.
   → Fix: invoke a Python interpreter directly on the script for scheduled runs
   (`_run_argv` / `_scheduled_python`), never the `uv run` shebang.

2. **`import plistlib` → `pyexpat.so` stalls in amfid.** Loading a C-extension
   `.so` triggers macOS `amfid` code-signature verification, which can deadlock
   under a daemon bootstrap (and `amfid` got wedged by repeated rapid launches).
   → Fix: `plistlib` is only needed by `install` (always interactive); make it a
   lazy import so the scheduled `run` hot path never loads it.

3. **The uv-managed Python lives on a secondary volume.** `lsof` showed the
   interpreter at `/Volumes/Data/.../uv-share/python/cpython-*/bin/python3.11`
   (a separate device). Memory-mapping its binary / `.so` files from that volume
   BLOCKS in `dyld mapFileReadOnly` under a daemon bootstrap — a volume-access
   gate the GUI session has but daemons don't. A trivial `python -c print` from
   the same interpreter ran fine; the full import set hung.
   → Fix: `_scheduled_python()` prefers a **main-volume** interpreter
   (`/opt/homebrew/bin/python3`); the script is stdlib-only so any 3.11+ works.

4. **claude's TUI renders NOTHING in a daemon-created tmux server.** After the
   hangs were gone the run completed but the pane was blank: claude launched in a
   tmux server that a daemon created draws nothing (same env, same flags), and
   the session dies. But a daemon that CONNECTS to the user's already-running
   GUI-session tmux server and spawns claude *there* renders perfectly.
   → Fix: `run` injects a transient `warmup-<ts>` session into the user's
   **default** tmux server (no private `-L` socket) and kills only that session.

## How to tell which trap you hit

- Stuck PID is `uv`, no log → trap 1.
- Stuck `python`, `sample` in `mapFileReadOnly`, interpreter path under
  `/Volumes/...` → trap 3 (or trap 2 if it loaded a `.so` like `pyexpat`).
- Run finishes, log written, `/usage` panel empty → trap 4.

## Verify

\```bash
agent-warmup at --delay 60s --verify     # pueue (daemon) path
# then read the newest ~/.cache/agent-warmup/run-*.log:
#   status: ok  AND a populated "## /usage panel" with "Current session ... Resets"
#   = claude rendered and the 5h subscription window advanced.
\```

A `status: warning: blank pane` line (added by the fix) means trap 4 recurred —
check that a tmux server is running in the GUI session.

## Constraint that remains

The warmup borrows the GUI-session tmux server, so **a tmux server must be
running in the login session at warmup time**. If none exists and the caller is
not a TTY, `run` notifies and exits (it will not spawn a daemon-owned server,
which would only reproduce trap 4).

## References

- [docs/tools/agent-warmup.md](../docs/tools/agent-warmup.md)
- [headless-claude-p-does-not-move-5h-window.md](headless-claude-p-does-not-move-5h-window.md) (the billing reason warmup must be interactive at all)
- [backlog/agent-quota-warmup-at-time.md](../backlog/agent-quota-warmup-at-time.md)

80	## Backends
81	
82	| Schedule | macOS | Linux |
83	|---|---|---|
84	| Recurring (`install`) | `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.<user>.agent-warmup.plist` (`StartCalendarInterval`), loaded with `launchctl bootstrap`; validated with `plutil -lint` | `~/.config/systemd/user/agent-warmup.{service,timer}` (`OnCalendar=`, `Persistent=true`), `systemctl --user enable --now`; validated with `systemd-analyze verify` |

87	The recurring timer is **imperative and opt-in** — generated by `install`, it is
88	*not* chezmoi-managed (so there is no `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` prompt and no forced
89	install on every machine). Run `install` on the host where you want the warmup.
90	
91	## Caveats
92	
93	- **Machine asleep at the scheduled time** → the job fires on wake (launchd
94	  coalesces missed calendar events; systemd uses `Persistent=true`), so the
95	  window geometry shifts to wake time.
96	- **Keychain must be unlocked** (you must be logged into the GUI session) for
97	  subscription auth to work from launchd/systemd.
98	- **Auth expiry** → if the session can't authenticate, `run` logs the capture
99	  and fires a desktop notification rather than typing into a dead session.
100	
101	## Relationship to `agent-wakeup`
102	
103	`agent-warmup` is a **separate** tool from
104	[`agent-wakeup`](agent-panes-discovery.md) (quota *recovery* — scheduling a
105	`continue` into an existing blocked pane). Warmup needs no existing pane, starts
106	a fresh isolated session, and must not continue real work. The broader

你原本覺得 Codex 那版「實現得不太好」是對的 —— 但真正的難點不在那,而在**背景排程跑 claude TUI** 撞到一連串 macOS daemon 行為,每修好一層才看得到下一層:

       def _scheduled_python() -> str:

           for cand in candidates:

Claude was alive but its TUI rendered nothing in a server the daemon created. Fixed by injecting into the USER'S EXISTING DEFAULT tmux server (no `-L` socket) — proven by probe: daemon → default server → claude renders perfectly.

   - **False `status: ok` on blank pane**: Added blank-capture detection: if `capture.strip()` is empty, write `status: warning: blank pane` and notify.

5. Problem Solving:

   **Solved**: The complete unattended warmup path now works:
   - pueue one-shot (daemon) → injects into default tmux server → claude renders → replies → `/usage` captured → `status: ok`, Claude Max, "Current session" 5h bucket, Usage credits off
   - launchd recurring timer → same mechanism → also verified working

   **Understanding gained**: The fundamental constraint is that claude's TUI requires a tmux server that was created by a GUI login session. The solution borrows the existing server rather than creating a new one. This means tmux must be running at warmup time.
